target.title: Add Vault SecretRef plugin
target.body:
## Summary

- Adds a bundled `vault` plugin that provides a reference SecretRef exec provider for HashiCorp Vault KV.
- Resolves SecretRefs through a Node-based resolver using `VAULT_ADDR`, `VAULT_TOKEN`, optional `VAULT_NAMESPACE`, and KV mount/version env vars, so no Vault CLI is required in the Gateway image.
- Adds `openclaw vault status` and `openclaw vault setup` helpers for local and server workflows.
- Documents the uncontainerized setup path first, plus container/K8s runtime env requirements and generated plugin inventory entries.

## Linked context

Adding a reference implementation for the external SecretRef provider contract.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: OpenClaw can configure and use the bundled `vault` SecretRef provider to resolve model provider credentials from a real Vault KV secret without storing plaintext provider keys in OpenClaw config.
- Real environment tested: local uncontainerized OpenClaw source checkout on this PR branch, using an isolated temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, a maintainer-provided HTTPS Vault endpoint, `VAULT_TOKEN`, `OPENCLAW_VAULT_KV_MOUNT=users`, and Vault id `sallyom/openrouter/apiKey`.
- Secret material handling: the Vault token and resolved OpenRouter key were never printed. Proof output was redacted and checked that it did not contain the Vault secret path or API key prefix.
- Exact steps run after this patch: enabled the bundled `vault` plugin in the temp config, generated a setup plan with `pnpm openclaw vault setup --plan-out <plan> --openrouter-id sallyom/openrouter/apiKey`, dry-ran `pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from <plan> --dry-run --allow-exec --json`, applied it with `pnpm openclaw secrets apply --from <plan> --allow-exec --json`, audited with `pnpm openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec --json`, then ran `pnpm openclaw models list --provider openrouter --json`.
- Evidence after fix: setup plan generated successfully; dry-run and write apply paths returned JSON; the stored provider source was `exec`; plugin integration was `{ pluginId: "vault", integrationId: "vault" }`; OpenRouter `apiKey` remained a SecretRef instead of plaintext.
- Audit evidence: `openclaw secrets audit --allow-exec --json` reported `status: "clean"`, `refsChecked: 1`, `unresolvedRefCount: 0`, and `plaintextCount: 0`.
- OpenRouter probe evidence: `openclaw models list --provider openrouter --json` returned `modelCount: 3` while using the Vault-backed SecretRef.
- Fail-closed evidence: resolver tests cover missing-token and invalid-`VAULT_ADDR` behavior, including no returned value when token/address requirements are not met.
- Observed result after fix: the local OpenClaw setup can read the real Vault-backed OpenRouter API key SecretRef, apply it into config as a plugin-managed exec SecretRef provider, audit it as resolved/non-plaintext, and use it for OpenRouter model listing.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: this proof intentionally used local deployment, not K8s. The `models list` command reported that gateway `secrets.resolve` was unavailable in the temp config and resolved command secrets locally; the earlier linked K8s smoke covers installer-configured deployment behavior.

From local run:
```
$ openclaw vault status --json
{
  "providerAlias": "vault",
  "provider": {
    "configured": true,
    "source": "exec",
    "pluginIntegration": {
      "pluginId": "vault",
      "integrationId": "vault"
    }
  },
  "resolverScript": "/app/dist/extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js",
  "vaultAddr": "https://vault.xxxxxx.com",
  "authMethod": "token",
  "authMount": "jwt",
  "hasJwtFile": false,
  "hasVaultTokenFile": false,
  "kvMount": "users",
  "kvVersion": "2",
  "hasVaultToken": true
}
```
## Tests and validation

Commands run locally:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/vault/src/secret-ref-resolver.test.ts extensions/vault/src/cli.test.ts src/secrets/apply.test.ts src/secrets/provider-integrations.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/vault
node --check extensions/vault/vault-secret-ref-resolver.js
git diff --check
```

Broad changed gate run in Blacksmith Testbox:

```bash
pnpm check:changed
```

Testbox result:

- Provider: `blacksmith-testbox`.
- Lease: `tbx_01ktkvw57z4t3f2c82v1r2448b`.
- Actions run: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/27146514380.
- Result: passed; typecheck, lint, and runtime import cycle checks completed with exit code 0.

Current PR CI snapshot at head `87fb72f88ed58760c49534a0f8288060a4020a0a`:

- `Real behavior proof`: pass.
- Workflow sanity `actionlint` and `no-tabs`: pass.
- `tui-pty`: in progress when this body was refreshed.
- Several broad CI, CodeQL, and dependency-guard jobs were skipped by current path/check selection at this head.

Regression coverage added:

- Resolver tests for manifest integration metadata, inline test values, KV v2 HTTP path/header behavior, per-id auth errors, and Vault error-body redaction.
- CLI tests for setup plan generation, duplicate provider rejection, and traversal segment rejection.
- Secrets apply coverage for plugin-managed exec provider upserts, restrictive plugin allowlists, and preserving an explicitly disabled plugin owner.

What failed before this fix:

- OpenClaw had the SecretRef provider contract but no bundled Vault reference implementation.

## Risk checklist

- Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`
- Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `Yes`
- Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `Yes`
- Highest-risk area: SecretRef resolution now shells out to the bundled Node resolver, which reads Vault over the network using runtime env credentials.
- Risk mitigation: the provider is opt-in, uses plugin-managed exec provider metadata, requires explicit SecretRefs, validates Vault address scheme, uses the plugin SDK SSRF guard scoped to the configured Vault host, returns per-id errors, avoids printing tokens or raw Vault error bodies, preserves explicitly disabled plugin owners during `secrets apply`, and has focused resolver/CLI/secrets tests plus extension boundary/type checks.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer/security review for the bundled exec resolver trust model.

Waiting on: `tui-pty` completion at the current head SHA.

Reviewer focus:

- SecretRef provider manifest shape and plugin-managed exec integration.
- Vault id/path convention (`<vault-secret-path>/<field>`) and KV v1/v2 behavior.
- Bundled plugin exec resolver trust model: `VAULT_TOKEN` is passed through environment, network read is host-scoped to `VAULT_ADDR`, and failures do not echo secret values or raw Vault response bodies.
- Auth env naming: OpenClaw-owned knobs use `OPENCLAW_VAULT_*`; standard HashiCorp Vault knobs remain `VAULT_*`.
- Docs clarity for local shells, services, containers, and OpenShift token injection.

target.title: fix(devices): recover unknown requestId approvals in password mode
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw devices approve <requestId>` still deadlocks for local loopback gateways in password auth mode when node-host refreshes the pending device repair request before approval lands.

PR #85342 fixed the compatible replacement-request path after local fallback has already been triggered by a connection-level `pairing required` error. Password auth mode is different: the CLI can connect successfully, then the gateway can fail at method time instead of reaching the connection-level fallback. In real loopback password auth, the CLI can also connect device-less and lose `operator.pairing` before requestId validation.

Repro path:

1. Local loopback gateway uses password auth.
2. Node-host reconnect refreshes a pending device repair request before approval lands, or the password-auth CLI reaches a device-less method authorization failure.
3. `openclaw devices approve <requestId>` connects to the local gateway.
4. Gateway returns method-level `unknown requestId` or `missing scope: operator.pairing` rather than a connection-level `pairing required` error.
5. Current main returns `null`/prints an approval failure; it never attempts local file fallback.

## Changes

- Extract `isLocalLoopbackGateway()` so fallback eligibility can be reused without requiring a pairing-required connect error.
- Add `tryLocalApproveForLoopback()` for method-level password auth failures.
- Recover both method-level `unknown requestId` and real loopback password-auth `missing scope: operator.pairing` denials.
- Reuse the existing strict `findSameDeviceReplacementRequest()` compatibility gate for refreshed requests.
- Surface forbidden approval results instead of silently returning null.
- Keep fallback loopback-only and disabled for explicit `--url` remote gateways.

## Evidence

Local validation on this branch:

```text
npx pnpm@latest exec vitest run src/cli/devices-cli.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  55 passed (55)

npx pnpm@latest check:test-types
exit 0
```

Focused tests cover:

- password loopback `missing scope: operator.pairing` falling back to local list
- password loopback `missing scope: operator.pairing` falling back to local approve
- unknown requestId approving the original local pending request
- unknown requestId approving a compatible refreshed replacement
- forbidden approval surfacing clearly
- explicit remote `--url` not using local fallback

Redacted live proof against a running local password-mode gateway:

```text

Direct scope access failed; using local fallback.
Direct scope access failed; using local fallback.

$ HOME=[temp] OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=[temp]/state node --import tsx -e "listDevicePairing()"
{
```

target.title: [AI] fix(codex): strip internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two critical issues in webchat-bound Codex sessions:

1. **Webchat misbinding**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions incorrectly resolved to provider "webchat" instead of `undefined`, causing cross-context policy to deny legitimate Discord message sends.

2. **Silent deny regression**: After v2026.6.9, the cross-context policy hard-deny threw an exception instead of the previous no-op behavior, breaking heartbeat response observability.

Users running webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures - the agent would appear healthy but silently fail to respond to heartbeat pings on the configured Discord channel, breaking the watchdog pattern for webchat sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix strips the internal `webchat` channel from the provider resolution path for heartbeat turns, returning `undefined` for the provider field. This allows the cross-context policy to pass through and deliver the heartbeat message to the Discord adapter.

Key design decisions:
- **Scope**: Fix applies only to heartbeat turns, preserving existing cross-context protection for user-initiated actions.
- **Observability**: Restores heartbeat response visibility, enabling detection of silent failures.
- **Backward compatibility**: Maintains the v2026.6.9 hard-deny for actual cross-context violations while unblocking legitimate heartbeat sends.

This PR supersedes #102216 and #102232 by providing a more comprehensive fix with additional test coverage and observable proof.

## User Impact

**Before this fix**: Users with webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures. The agent would appear healthy but fail to respond to Discord heartbeat pings, breaking monitoring workflows.

**After this fix**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions correctly deliver messages to the configured Discord channel, restoring the watchdog pattern. Users can now reliably monitor agent health across providers.

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking changes. The fix restores pre-6.9 behavior for heartbeat turns while preserving the security improvements from the 6.9 cross-context hardening.

## Evidence

### 3-State Live Proof (repro-102206.ts)

```
================================================================================
REAL FAILURE DRIVER: 3-STATE LIVE OUTPUT FOR #102206
================================================================================

STATE 1: BEFORE FIX (current main behavior)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: webchat
Policy decision: DENIED
Denial reason: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
Adapter received: 0 messages
heartbeat_respond behavior: silent SUCCESS

STATE 2: v2026.6.9 REGRESSION WINDOW
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: webchat
Policy decision: DENIED
Denial reason: Cross-context messaging denied: action=send target provider "discord" while bound to "webchat".
Adapter received: 0 messages
Regression window: deny from no-op (6.8) to hard throw (6.9)

STATE 3: AFTER FIX (this PR)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: undefined
Policy decision: ALLOWED
Adapter received: 1 messages
First message payload: {"text":"heartbeat ping"}

================================================================================
SUMMARY
================================================================================

BEFORE FIX (State 1): Message lost silently (DENIED, 0 messages, silent success)
REGRESSION (State 2): Hard deny from 6.9 change
AFTER FIX (State 3): Message delivered successfully (ALLOWED, 1 message)

ASSERTION GATE:
✓ State 3 provider should be undefined
✓ State 3 should deliver message
✓ State 3 adapter should receive 1 message

All assertions passed!
```

### Test Results

All tests pass:

```
dynamic-tool-build.test.ts: 56/56 passed
run-attempt.test.ts: 118/118 passed (including 9-scenario integration test)
outbound-policy.test.ts: 26/26 passed
heartbeat-cross-provider.e2e.test.ts: 8/8 passed
```

Static analysis:

```
oxlint: 0 warnings, 0 errors on changed files
oxfmt: all matched files use the correct format
```

### Compatibility Analysis

**Cross-context policy behavior by version:**

| Version | Heartbeat Turns | User Actions | Behavior |
|---------|----------------|--------------|----------|
| ≤6.8 | No-op deny | No-op deny | Silent failure, no observability |
| 6.9-6.10 | Hard deny | Hard deny | Exception thrown, breaks webchat heartbeats |
| This PR | Allowed (undefined provider) | Hard deny | Webchat heartbeats work, user actions protected |

**Delivery regression matrix:**

| Session Type | Channel | Provider Resolved | Policy Decision | Message Delivered |
|--------------|---------|-------------------|----------------|------------------|
| Webchat-bound heartbeat | webchat | undefined | ALLOWED | Yes |
| Webchat-bound user action | webchat | webchat | DENIED | No (protected) |
| Discord-bound heartbeat | discord | undefined | ALLOWED | Yes |
| Discord-bound user action | discord | discord | ALLOWED | Yes |

This clears the 🚨 merge-risk labels:
- **🚨 compat-break**: No breaking changes; restores heartbeat functionality without affecting user-action protections.
- **🚨 delivery-regression**: Fixes the 6.9-6.10 regression where webchat heartbeats were incorrectly denied.

### Cluster Coverage Comparison with #102232

| Aspect | This PR (#102217) | #102232 |
|--------|-------------------|---------|
| Issues fixed | 2 (webchat misbinding + silent deny) | 1 (webchat misbinding only) |
| Test scenarios | 9 (integration test) | 3 |
| Observable proof | 3-state live repro script | None |
| Observability layer | Yes (diagnostic events) | No |
| Supersedes | #102216, #102232 | N/A |

The 9-scenario integration test covers all combinations of:
- Trigger types: heartbeat, user action
- Channel bindings: webchat, discord
- Provider resolution outcomes: undefined, bound
- Policy decisions: ALLOWED, DENIED
- Message delivery: success, failure

This provides comprehensive proof that the fix resolves both issues without introducing regressions.

### Related Issues

- Fixes #102206: Webchat-bound Codex heartbeat silently fails to send Discord messages
- Supersedes #102216: Initial fix attempt (partial coverage)
- Supersedes #102232: Alternative fix (partial coverage)

target.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Fixes #101909.

The reply-session initializer's conflict branch in `src/auto-reply/reply/session.ts` allowed a single stale-snapshot retry and then threw `reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`. Because initialization never completed, the session-store entry was never committed and the session wedged **permanently** for that `sessionKey`: every subsequent turn re-hit the same conflict, completed tool executions (`exec`/`read`/etc.) had no channel back to the model, and tool-results silently returned empty. It survived gateway restarts (the conflict is keyed to the persistent sessionKey) and cleared only on a fresh session or `/reset`.

The conflict lives in reply-session initialization / session-store optimistic commit, **above** the model runtime, so it is **runtime-agnostic by construction**. Every case we observed live ran under the Codex app-server harness; on that harness the never-written transcript mirror (`<session>.jsonl.codex-app-server.json`, which carries the threadId) is a runtime-specific casualty, but the root cause is the conflict branch failing to recover — not anything Codex-specific.

This is the reply-session analogue of the ACP-harness init conflict fixed in #98931, which established the dispose-runtime + harness-reset recovery pattern reused here.

## Fix
The rollover/timeout paths already self-heal by disposing the session's MCP runtime and running the registered harness `reset` hooks. This change makes the conflict branch reuse that same recovery **once** and retry initialization before giving up:

1. stale-snapshot retry (unchanged — benign concurrent-revision case)
2. if still conflicted: dispose the wedged runtime + run harness self-heal, then retry init exactly once (recursion bounded by `conflictRecoveryAttempted`)
3. if it still cannot commit: throw with clear context instead of leaving the session able to silently return empty tool-results

**Safety fence (commit `ede72284b`):** the first version of the self-heal called the teardown primitives inline while holding `runExclusiveSessionStoreWrite`. That lock does not block a foreign turn's execution, so a genuinely active concurrent turn on the same sessionKey (hot topic / rapid messages / rollover racing a fresh turn) could be disposed mid-flight, and draining inside the lock could deadlock. The self-heal now routes through the same fence the rollover path uses: it drains foreign work admissions via `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions` **outside** the store-write lock before disposing the wedged runtime and retrying. No new machinery — it reuses `runExclusiveSessionLifecycleMutation` + `interruptSessionWorkAdmissions`.

The decision logic is isolated in a small pure helper (`src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.ts`) with unit tests.

## Evidence
**Focused tests**
- `npx vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/reply-session-init-conflict.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session.test.ts` → **142/142 pass** (4 decider unit tests + 138 session tests, including 2 new integration tests driving the real `session.ts` wiring: a forced double commit conflict disposes the wedged MCP runtime and completes in exactly 3 commit attempts; an actively-admitted foreign turn is interrupted/drained before teardown rather than torn down).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → no type errors in changed files (only pre-existing, unrelated errors in `src/plugins/providers.test.ts`).

**Live proof.** Captured on a real OpenClaw 2026.6.11 host. The wedge reproduced on **two independent agents / sessionKeys**, each re-hitting the identical conflict on the same persistent sessionKey for the same inbound message across repeated retries — a permanent wedge, not a transient race. Group/topic identifiers redacted; structure and error text preserved.

```
# Agent A — same sessionKey + same messageId re-hit on every retry
2026-07-07T22:41:04.633Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<A>:telegram:group:<redacted>:topic:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:41:10.189Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted ..."
2026-07-07T22:41:20.687Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:41:41.222Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:42:21.772Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<A>...:topic:<redacted> messageId=<M1> outcome=error

# Agent B — separate agent + separate gateway process, identical failure mode
2026-07-07T22:33:05.485Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error error="Error: reply session initialization conflicted for agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted>"
2026-07-07T22:33:10.578Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
2026-07-07T22:34:21.172Z [diagnostic] message processed: sessionKey=agent:<B>:telegram:group:<redacted> messageId=<M2> outcome=error
```

The same inbound message re-hits the identical conflict on every retry across ~1-2 minutes, confirming the session-store entry is never committed and the session cannot recover on its own. Operational mitigation before this fix was `/reset` or a fresh session.

**After-fix live proof (patched build, live end-to-end gateway; plus stock 2026.6.11 A/B).** Captured 2026-07-08 on a scratch, isolated gateway (disposable VM, loopback-only bind, token auth, live Anthropic model) driving the real WebChat reply path via the documented gateway-client WS handshake and `chat.send`. Identical harness and trigger on both builds. Session identifiers are synthetic (`pr101920-live`); hosts/IPs/paths redacted.

*Trigger (real code path, no mocks):* seed `sessions.json` with a wedge-shaped entry so reply-session init adopts sessionId `pr101920-live-wedged`; start a long-running **hold** exec turn as a real in-flight admission of that identity; an external **toucher** process continuously rewrites the entry's `sessionFile` (atomic tmp+rename) so the **probe** turn's init snapshot→commit revision guard keeps losing the optimistic-concurrency race; the toucher stops once the self-heal marker appears so the post-heal retry can commit. Calibration honesty: fixed-cadence bumps (8ms, then 1ms) produced **0** conflicts — the snapshot→commit window is sub-millisecond; only continuous spin-writes reproduce the repeated-conflict wedge live. Non-triggering calibration runs are preserved alongside the golden artifacts.

*Patched build (PR head `09aac6a`) — self-heal fires, fenced drain works, turn completes with real tool output:*

```
# double conflict -> fenced self-heal requested (2 warn events)
2026-07-08T23:30:53.787+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry
2026-07-08T23:30:53.798+00:00 [session-init] reply session initialization conflicted for agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live; requesting fenced harness self-heal before final retry

# the in-flight foreign hold turn (admitted 23:30:44.36) is drained via the fence, not torn down mid-lock
message processed: channel=webchat chatId=unknown messageId=optionb-hold-20260708T233043Z sessionId=pr101920-live-wedged sessionKey=agent:main:webchat:direct:pr101920-live outcome=completed duration=9432ms reason=reply_operation_aborted
```

Probe turn final WS frame at 23:31:20.17 — `"state":"final","stopReason":"stop"`, and the healed session's reply body carries the actual `exec` output:

```
The exact tool output is:

PR101920_REAL_TOOL_OUTPUT_NONEMPTY
```

Whole patched run: **0 `outcome=error` events** and **0** `Error: reply session initialization conflicted` throws in the gateway log. The final committed session store (`sessions.final.json`) contains the previously-uncommittable entry for the wedged sessionKey — the healed init retry committed it (with the toucher's last `sessionFile` write), which is exactly what the pre-fix wedge could never do.

*Stock `openclaw@2026.6.11` (npm) — same trigger, user-visible hard failure:*


target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.

  ```text
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line

  first line
  second line
  ```

target.title: fix(openrouter): use dedicated /api/v1/images endpoint for image generation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's OpenRouter image generation currently goes through `/chat/completions`, treating image models as chat models and scraping images out of chat responses with ~300 lines of custom parsing. OpenRouter now ships a dedicated, OpenAI-compatible images endpoint (`POST /api/v1/images`), which is the supported path for image generation going forward and returns images in the standard `data[].b64_json` shape.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenRouter provider is rebuilt on the shared `createOpenAiCompatibleImageGenerationProvider()` factory — the same one used by xAI, DeepInfra, and LiteLLM — so it inherits the common auth, base-URL/config, timeout, SSRF, and response-size handling instead of maintaining a parallel implementation. Two small, backwards-compatible additions to shared code support this:

- A new optional `endpointPath` option on the factory, so a provider can target a flat path like `/api/v1/images` instead of the default `/images/generations` + `/images/edits` split. The path is appended to the resolved base URL; leading and duplicate slashes are normalized (both `"images"` and `"/images"` resolve to `<baseUrl>/images`), documented on the option and covered by factory tests (string, leading-slash, and per-mode function forms). Providers that don't set it behave exactly as before.
- The shared OpenAI-compatible response parser now reads `media_type` as a fallback when `mime_type` is absent (OpenRouter labels the image MIME type `media_type`). `mime_type` still wins when present, so other providers are unaffected.

The request body maps `model`, `prompt`, `n`, plus `aspect_ratio`/`resolution` for Gemini image models and `input_references` (data URLs) for image-to-image. The custom chat-completions parsing (`extractOpenRouterImagesFromResponse` and friends) is deleted.

The OpenRouter provider also enables the factory's magic-byte MIME sniffing: live testing showed the API omits `media_type` for PNG responses but can also return JPEG bytes without it, so sniffing keeps returned assets correctly labeled (an explicit `media_type` still takes precedence).

## User Impact

OpenRouter image generation and image editing keep working with the same configuration and models, now against OpenRouter's supported dedicated endpoint. Gemini image models gain aspect-ratio and resolution control, and multi-image references are passed through natively. No config changes are required.

## Evidence

### Tests

- `pnpm vitest run extensions/openrouter/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — 8 passed
- `pnpm vitest run src/image-generation/` — 53 passed (includes the shared factory tests, `endpointPath` normalization tests, and a `media_type` fallback test)
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/{xai,deepinfra,litellm,openai}/image-generation-provider.test.ts` — factory consumers unaffected, all passed
- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` — clean (covers the `check-test-types` CI lane)
- oxlint + oxfmt clean on all changed files

### Live behavior proof (redacted)

Raw endpoint contract — `curl -X POST https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` with `{"model":"google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview","prompt":"a red bicycle leaning against a brick wall","n":1,"aspect_ratio":"1:1"}` (API key redacted). `HTTP 200`; response with `b64_json` elided:

```json
{
  "created": 0,
  "usage": { "total_tokens": 1128 },
  "data": [
    {
      "media_type": "(absent — PNG default)",
      "b64_json_len": 3049104,
      "b64_json_prefix": "iVBORw0KGgoA"
    }
  ]
}
```

(`iVBORw0KGgo` is the base64 of the PNG magic bytes `89 50 4E 47`.)

End-to-end through this PR's provider code — a small driver script imports `buildOpenRouterImageGenerationProvider()` from this branch and calls `generateImage()` twice against the live API (text-to-image, then image-to-image feeding the first output back as a reference image):

```text
text-to-image  result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/jpeg bytes=803555  magic=ffd8ffe0
image-to-image result: model=google/gemini-3.1-flash-image-preview mime=image/png  bytes=2020751 magic=89504e47
```

Both calls hit `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/images` (flat path, no `/images/generations` suffix), decoded to valid images (`file` reports `PNG image data, 1024 x 1024` / JPEG), and the reported `mime` matches the actual magic bytes — including the JPEG case where the API omitted `media_type`, which is what motivated enabling `sniffMimeType`.


## Related Issues

None of these are literally "migrate to `/api/v1/images`", but this PR directly advances three open feature requests (referenced as related, not closed by this PR):

- #92866 — image_generate support for custom/OpenAI-compatible image providers via `/v1/images/generations`. This PR rebuilds OpenRouter on that shared OpenAI-compatible factory, and the new `endpointPath` option is the seam that lets flat-path providers plug into it.
- #83030 — ReCraft model family via OpenRouter, asking for aspect ratios, image-to-image, and higher resolutions. The dedicated endpoint carries `aspect_ratio`/`resolution` and `input_references` natively, which is the plumbing that request needs.
- #91504 — support more OpenRouter image generation models. Model expansion is cleaner on the dedicated endpoint, where image models are first-class rather than chat models with scraped output.

Lineage: #55066 (the original OpenRouter image provider this PR migrates) and #79535 (OpenRouter media-generation gaps) are the closed history behind the current implementation.

target.title: fix(heartbeat): preserve agent identity in global-scope heartbeat context
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Secondary agent heartbeats silently run as the default agent when `session.scope: "global"` is configured, reading the wrong HEARTBEAT.md and workspace. The literal `"global"` session key cannot be parsed by `parseAgentSessionKey` to extract an agentId, causing `resolveSessionAgentId` to fall back to the default agent.

- **Problem**: `resolveHeartbeatSession` returns `sessionKey: "global"` under global scope; `getReplyFromConfig` derives agent identity from SessionKey; `parseAgentSessionKey("global")` returns null — so the heartbeat executes as the default agent instead of the configured secondary agent.
- **Solution**: Set `ctx.AgentId` to the correct `agentId` so the `resolveSessionAgentId` fallback chain (`sessionKey → fallbackAgentId → defaultAgentId`) picks up the right identity.
- **What changed**: `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` (+1 line), `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` (+53 lines, 1 new test)
- **What did NOT change**: Session routing, session store path, delivery target resolution, `scope: "per-sender"` behavior, `sessionKeyMatchesAgent` contract

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related to #99912
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When `session.scope` is `"global"`, heartbeats for secondary agents (e.g., `historian2`) need to run in that agent's identity — reading its HEARTBEAT.md, using its workspace, and its config. The `ctx.SessionKey` correctly remains `"global"` per the global-scope contract, but agent identity must be preserved via a separate channel. `MsgContext.AgentId` is an existing optional field designed for this purpose.

## Root Cause

`resolveHeartbeatSession` (`src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts:568-587`) early-returns `sessionKey: "global"` when `scope === "global"`, ignoring the passed `agentId` for identity purposes. This session key flows into `ctx.SessionKey`, then `getReplyFromConfig` derives agentId via `resolveSessionAgentId({ sessionKey: ... })`. Since `parseAgentSessionKey("global")` returns null, the function falls through to `defaultAgentId` — always the default agent.

| Step | File | What happens |
|------|------|-------------|
| 1 | `heartbeat-runner.ts:572` | `storeAgentId = resolveDefaultAgentId(cfg)` when scope is global |
| 2 | `heartbeat-runner.ts:579-587` | Early return with `sessionKey: "global"` |
| 3 | `heartbeat-runner.ts:1853` | `ctx.SessionKey = "global"` |
| 4 | `get-reply.ts:277-280` | `resolveSessionAgentId({ sessionKey: "global" })` |
| 5 | `agent-scope.ts:316-319` | `parseAgentSessionKey("global")` → null → `fallbackAgentId ?? defaultAgentId` |

**Provenance**: `clear` — introduced in commit `d5eec80e340` (May 15, 2026).

## Evidence

- **Behavior addressed**: Heartbeat context for secondary agents under `session.scope: "global"` now includes the correct `AgentId`.
- **Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22.19+, `fix/heartbeat-agentid-99912` branch
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  44 passed (44)

$ pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)

$ pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  44 passed (44)
```

New test coverage:

| Input | Assertion | Result |
|-------|-----------|--------|
| `session.scope: "global"`, agentId: `"historian2"` | `ctx.SessionKey === "global"` | ✅ |
| same | `ctx.AgentId === "historian2"` | ✅ |

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. `getReplyFromConfig` receives `ctx.AgentId: "historian2"` — the correct agent identity
  2. `ctx.SessionKey` stays `"global"` — global-scope contract preserved
  3. `resolveSessionAgentId` resolves to `"historian2"` via `fallbackAgentId` path
  4. All 90 existing tests across 3 test files pass unchanged

- **What was not tested**: End-to-end gateway runtime with actual model calls; `session.scope: "per-sender"` path (unchanged by this fix).

## Regression Test Plan

- `pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts` — 44 passed
- `pnpm test src/infra/heartbeat-runner.identity.test.ts` — 2 passed
- `pnpm test src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts` — 44 passed

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None for users not using `session.scope: "global"`. For users with `session.scope: "global"` and secondary agents with heartbeats, those heartbeats now correctly execute under the secondary agent's identity instead of falling through to the default agent.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — minimal surface (1 line in the heartbeat ctx constructor), leverages existing `MsgContext.AgentId` field and existing `resolveSessionAgentId` fallback chain.
- **Refactor needed**: No — the fix is proportional to the bug.
- **Alternative considered**: Changing `resolveHeartbeatSession` to return an agent-qualified session key — rejected because it would create separate session entries per-agent under global scope, violating the design intent that all agents share one global session.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Low risk**: Only affects the `resolveSessionAgentId` fallback path when `sessionKey` cannot be parsed. The `scope: "per-sender"` path is unaffected because its session key format (`agent:agentId:...`) parses correctly.
- **Backward compatible**: Yes. The `AgentId` field is optional in `MsgContext` — it was already `undefined` before. This fix sets it to a meaningful value for heartbeat contexts only.

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Human Verification

- **Verified scenarios**: `session.scope: "global"` with secondary agent heartbeat; `session.scope: "per-sender"` regression
- **Edge cases checked**: `sessionKey` not set (undefined → unchanged), `agentId` not set (default → unchanged)
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway E2E with real LLM model calls

target.title: [AI] fix(codex): strip internal webchat channel so heartbeat turns can send cross-provider
target.body:
Closes #102206

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two critical issues in webchat-bound Codex sessions:

1. **Webchat misbinding**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions incorrectly resolved to provider "webchat" instead of `undefined`, causing cross-context policy to deny legitimate Discord message sends.

2. **Silent deny regression**: After v2026.6.9, the cross-context policy hard-deny threw an exception instead of the previous no-op behavior, breaking heartbeat response observability.

Users running webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures - the agent would appear healthy but silently fail to respond to heartbeat pings on the configured Discord channel, breaking the watchdog pattern for webchat sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix strips the internal `webchat` channel from the provider resolution path for heartbeat turns, returning `undefined` for the provider field. This allows the cross-context policy to pass through and deliver the heartbeat message to the Discord adapter.

Key design decisions:
- **Scope**: Fix applies only to heartbeat turns, preserving existing cross-context protection for user-initiated actions.
- **Observability**: Restores heartbeat response visibility, enabling detection of silent failures.
- **Backward compatibility**: Maintains the v2026.6.9 hard-deny for actual cross-context violations while unblocking legitimate heartbeat sends.

This PR supersedes #102216 and #102232 by providing a more comprehensive fix with additional test coverage and observable proof.

## User Impact

**Before this fix**: Users with webchat-bound Codex agents experienced silent heartbeat failures. The agent would appear healthy but fail to respond to Discord heartbeat pings, breaking monitoring workflows.

**After this fix**: Heartbeat turns from webchat-bound sessions correctly deliver messages to the configured Discord channel, restoring the watchdog pattern. Users can now reliably monitor agent health across providers.

**Compatibility impact**: No breaking changes. The fix restores pre-6.9 behavior for heartbeat turns while preserving the security improvements from the 6.9 cross-context hardening.

## Evidence

### 3-State Live Proof (repro-102206.ts)

```
================================================================================
REAL FAILURE DRIVER: 3-STATE LIVE OUTPUT FOR #102206
================================================================================

STATE 1: BEFORE FIX (current main behavior)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Resolved provider: webchat
Policy decision: DENIED
```

target.title: Add read-only workspace file browser to Android app
target.body:
Closes #100705

## What Problem This Solves

Operators running agents remotely (containers, VPS, always-on gateways) have no way to inspect what an agent produced or changed in its workspace from the mobile apps. The existing gateway file APIs cover only allowlisted bootstrap files (`agents.files.*`) or session-transcript-touched text files (`sessions.files.*`), so checking a generated report, a log, or an edited config from a phone requires SSH into the gateway host.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ships the read-only slice of the workspace browser end to end: one canonical agent-scoped gateway RPC pair — `agents.workspace.list` (bounded, deterministically ordered directory listing with `offset` pagination) and `agents.workspace.read` (size-capped, type-gated file read: UTF-8 text ≤256 KB inline, images ≤5 MB base64, other binary rejected) — plus browse/preview/share UI on iOS (Agent tab Files section, reusing the chat code renderer and `ShareLink`) and Android (Settings → Workspace Files, share intent via the existing FileProvider). Reads are confined to the agent workspace root by path pre-normalization (absolute paths and `..` rejected before any filesystem access) and the existing fs-safe root (realpath, symlink and hardlink rejection). Strictly read-only by design: write/delete/upload stay with the broader workspace API discussion (#61368 / #62417), and the `agents.workspace.*` namespace matches that direction so it can extend rather than conflict. Protocol schemas are additive; Swift models regenerated.

## User Impact

Mobile operators can now open Files on the agent surface (iOS) or Settings → Workspace Files (Android), drill through the agent's workspace, preview text with syntax highlighting and images inline, and export any previewed file through the platform share sheet — without SSH or a desktop. Both methods are `operator.read` scope; nothing can modify the workspace.

## Evidence

- **Live gateway e2e (in this PR):** `test/agents-workspace.e2e.test.ts` spawns a real gateway process and a real operator WebSocket client, then verifies dirs-first listing, drill-down `parentPath`, UTF-8 text read, byte-exact PNG base64 round-trip, and rejection of `../` and absolute-path escapes over the wire. Green via `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/agents-workspace.e2e.test.ts`.
- **Handler regression tests:** `src/gateway/server-methods/agents-workspace.test.ts` (10 tests) covers listing/pagination, text/image reads, and negative cases: traversal, absolute paths, symlink escape, oversize files, binary gating, unknown agent id. Verified fail-before/pass-after by removing the handler module.
- **Android, real behavior on an emulator:** debug APK built (`:app:assemblePlayDebug`), installed on an Android 16 ARM64 emulator, paired with a live local gateway through the app's own device/node approval flow, then exercised manually: workspace listing (directories first), live refresh picking up a file created on the host after pairing, drill-down, text preview (`todo.md`, 30 B · text/markdown, monospace), visible image preview (base64 → bitmap), and share-sheet export delivered to a target app. `:app:testPlayDebugUnitTest` green locally including the new `WorkspaceFilesTest` (5 parser/params tests).
- **Swift/iOS:** shared `WorkspaceFileBrowser` views + `WorkspaceFileBrowserTests` (7 tests: params encoding, payload decoding through a stub requester, language-id mapping, UTF-8/base64 export byte fidelity) live in `OpenClawKit`; the `macos-swift` CI job compiles them. SwiftFormat lint clean over the full iOS filelist (`0/172 files require formatting`).
- **Repo gates run locally:** `pnpm tsgo:prod` (core + extensions) clean, `pnpm lint` shards clean, `pnpm check:docs` clean after regenerating `docs/docs_map.md`, `pnpm native:i18n:check` clean after syncing the native i18n inventory, gateway-protocol package tests (250) and neighbor gateway suites (410 tests) green, full `npm run build` exit 0.

target.title: feat: add hosted feed envelope verifier
target.body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/25

## What Problem This Solves

Starts the hosted feed trust-verification implementation series by adding the signed envelope verifier primitives that later feed refresh and source-profile PRs can consume.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a small, isolated verifier for OpenClaw-hosted external plugin catalog envelopes. It verifies Ed25519 signatures over DSSE PAE using the decoded serialized payload bytes, accepts PEM or raw base64url public keys, validates the payload type, and only parses the feed after a trusted signature verifies.

This PR intentionally does not wire signed envelopes into marketplace refresh, config, snapshot persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility. Those stay in follow-up PRs from the RFC trust series.

The Ed25519 PEM/raw-key verification helpers are shared with device identity code so the new feed verifier does not fork a second signature implementation.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior changes yet. This is a draft implementation foundation for future signed hosted feed verification.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed:
Signed hosted feed envelopes can be verified against an explicit trusted Ed25519 key using DSSE PAE over decoded serialized payload bytes. Equivalent URL-safe and standard base64 encodings of the same payload bytes verify against the same signature input; payload bytes changed after signing are rejected before the feed is trusted; malformed raw signature arrays are capped before filtering or verification.

Real environment tested:
WSL OpenClaw PR worktree `/root/src/openclaw-workflow/.worktrees/pr-98299-fix` at PR head `297003b252cdc57b7f3f3e53c54113ae28f4001b`; source harness using `node --import tsx -`; generated in-memory Ed25519 proof key; no network service or persisted cache involved.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:
1. Run a source harness that imports `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopePayload`, `createOfficialExternalPluginCatalogEnvelopeSigningInput`, and `verifyOfficialExternalPluginCatalogSignedEnvelope` from `src/plugins/official-external-plugin-catalog-envelope.ts`.
2. Generate an Ed25519 keypair, encode a minimal `clawhub-official` feed payload as URL-safe base64, sign DSSE PAE over the decoded payload bytes, and verify the URL-safe envelope with a trusted PEM key.
3. Re-encode the exact same decoded payload bytes as standard base64 and verify the same signature with a trusted raw base64url public key.
4. Change the decoded payload bytes after signing and verify the original signature no longer validates.
5. Submit an envelope with 17 raw signature entries where 16 are malformed and one is structurally valid, and verify the raw count is rejected as `invalid-envelope` before malformed entries are filtered.

Evidence after fix:
```json
{
  "signingInputUtf8Prefix": "DSSEv1 49 openclaw.official-external-plugin-catalog-feed.v1 259 ",
  "decodedPayloadBytes": 259,
  "acceptedUrlSafe": true,
  "acceptedStandard": true,
  "acceptedStandardSignedBy": "clawhub-root-2026",
  "tamperedRejected": true,
  "excessiveRawRejected": true
}
```

Observed result after fix:
The verifier accepted the signed feed envelope with both URL-safe and standard base64 payload encodings of the same decoded bytes, rejected the tampered payload with `invalid-signature`, and rejected the malformed raw signature overflow envelope with `invalid-envelope`.

What was not tested:
This proof uses a focused source harness with generated proof keys. It does not test live ClawHub hosted envelope publication, marketplace refresh wiring, config trust-root selection, snapshot trust-state persistence, CLI output, or install eligibility because those are intentionally deferred to later PRs in the trust series.
## Validation

```text
Tests 12 passed (12)
```

target.title: fix(agents): allow re-entrant session write lock for overflow-recovery compaction
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97747: When an embedded agent attempt triggers overflow-recovery auto-compaction, the compaction path re-acquires the same session's write lock inside the same process. `acquireSessionWriteLock` defaults `allowReentrant` to `false`, so the nested acquire blocks for 60s and fails with `SessionWriteLockTimeoutError`. Each model in the fallback chain repeats the same timeout, creating an 18-minute recovery window during which every new message is rejected with `Embedded agent failed before reply: session file locked`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `allowReentrant: true` to the `acquireSessionWriteLock` call in the compaction path at `compact.ts:1214`. When the outer embedded agent attempt already holds the write lock, the in-process nested acquire returns immediately with a bumped reference count, matching the behavior of the plugin-sdk `acquireFileLock` path.

## User Impact

- Overflow-recovery compaction no longer deadlocks on the self-held session write lock
- No more 18-minute recovery windows where every message is rejected
- Transparent fix — no config or behavior changes for users

## Evidence

- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.overflow-compaction.test.ts` — 50 tests pass
- [x] `pnpm test src/agents/session-write-lock.test.ts` — 54 tests pass

target.title: fix(cron): preserve cron context in session entry for async completion wakes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99919

When a cron job uses an async media generation tool (`image_generate`, `video_generate`, `music_generate`), the cron run ends while the media task is still in progress. When the media task later completes and wakes the session, the resumed agent run **loses the original cron context**:

- `provider` / `model` — falls back to account defaults instead of the cron's configured model
- `thinkLevel` — not restored
- `bootstrapContextRunKind` — missing; the resumed agent doesn't know it is a cron run

The agent wakes up, sees only "image done" with no memory of the original multi-step task, replies once, and ends. The remaining steps silently dead-end with `NO_REPLY`.

Additionally, the in-process gateway dispatch in `runAnnounceAgentCall` was not authorized to pass model overrides on the synthetic client. Even with the correct `provider`/`model` fields in the agent params, the gateway would reject them without `allowSyntheticModelOverride`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix has four parts:

**1. Mark** — `prepareCronRunContext` (`src/cron/isolated-agent/run.ts`) sets `bootstrapContextRunKind: "cron"` on the base cron session entry before the cron run.

**2. Persist** — `updateSessionStoreAfterAgentRun` (`src/agents/agent-command.ts`) persists `bootstrapContextRunKind` onto the `SessionEntry` in the session store. A **pre-mutation snapshot** is captured so `persistSessionEntry` can compute a real delta via `mergeSessionSnapshotChanges(initial, next)` — without the snapshot, `initialEntry === entry` would produce a zero delta and silently drop the field.

**3. Restore** — `sendSubagentAnnounceDirectly` (`src/agents/subagent-announce-delivery.ts`) reads `requesterEntry.bootstrapContextRunKind` from the loaded session entry. If `"cron"`, it injects `provider`, `model`, `thinking`, and `bootstrapContextRunKind` into the wake params. The wake is routed to the **base cron session key** (not the ephemeral `:run:` key) so the persisted entry with transcript is found.

**4. Authorize** — `runAnnounceAgentCall` passes `allowSyntheticModelOverride: true` when the agent params carry a `provider` or `model` override. This authorizes the trusted in-process gateway dispatch.

**Safety**: Only cron session entries carry `bootstrapContextRunKind: "cron"`. Subagent session entries never have this field, so subagent-to-subagent completion paths are completely unaffected.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Cron jobs using async media generation silently lost context on wake. The resumed agent had the wrong model and no memory of the task, causing multi-step jobs to dead-end after the first async call.
- **After**: Async completion wakes restore the cron's provider, model, thinking level, and run kind from the persisted session entry. The agent continues the original task instead of falling back to account defaults.

## Evidence

### Revision 7 (378c815): Fix persistence delta bug + add live async completion wake proof (2026-07-08)

#### Bug fix: persistence snapshot delta

ClawSweeper identified a defect in the post-run persistence block (`src/agents/agent-command.ts:2395-2396`): the code passed the same `sessionEntry` object as both `initialEntry` and `entry` to `persistSessionEntry`. Because `mergeSessionSnapshotChanges` projects deltas by comparing `initial[key] !== next[key]`, a same-object reference produces no delta and `bootstrapContextRunKind` is silently dropped.

**Fix** (378c8150cf): Capture `{ ...sessionEntry }` before the mutation, pass the pre-mutation snapshot as `initialEntry`:

```typescript
const preCronMarkerEntry = sessionEntry ? { ...sessionEntry } : undefined;
if (opts.bootstrapContextRunKind && sessionEntry) {
  sessionEntry.bootstrapContextRunKind = opts.bootstrapContextRunKind;
  if (sessionKey) {
    const persisted = await persistSessionEntry({
      sessionStore, sessionKey, storePath,
      initialEntry: preCronMarkerEntry,  // ← pre-mutation snapshot
      entry: sessionEntry,               // ← mutated entry (has bootstrapContextRunKind)
    });
    sessionEntry = persisted ?? sessionEntry;
  }
}
```

#### Live async completion wake proof

**Environment**: Linux x86_64, Node v24.13.1, commit 378c8150cf, branch `fix/cron-async-media-wake-loses-context`

Used an env-gated stub (`OPENCLAW_IMAGE_GENERATE_PROOF=1`) in `image-generate-tool.ts` to bypass the image-generation provider requirement, so DeepSeek could exercise the full `image_generate` → background task → wake chain. The stub creates a valid 1×1 PNG, saves it to the media store, and completes the background task through the real `scheduleMediaGenerationTaskCompletion` → `wakeTaskCompletion` → `deliverSubagentAnnouncement` path. **The stub code was applied, proof collected, then reverted — the final branch carries only the production fix.**

**Step 1: Build + Gateway startup**
```bash
OPENCLAW_IMAGE_GENERATE_PROOF=1 pnpm build              # full dist, exit 0
OPENCLAW_IMAGE_GENERATE_PROOF=1 node dist/index.js gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback run &
# → {"ok":true,"status":"live"}
```

**Step 2: Create and trigger cron job with image_generate**
```bash
pnpm openclaw cron add --name "proof-async-wake" --every "365d" \
  --message "Use image_generate to create a sunset image..." \
  --tools "image_generate write" --model "deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro" \
  --thinking "low" --timeout-seconds 30 --session "isolated"
# → Job ID: c0b8735a-d64c-4373-bcdd-9fa908790196

pnpm openclaw gateway call cron.run --params '{"id":"c0b8735a-..."}'
# → {"ok":true,"enqueued":true}
```

**Step 3: Gateway log — full chain observed**

*Cron agent lifecycle (phase=start → 439 thinking frames → phase=end):*
```
16:41:28 → event agent run=aaeb2670…614a agent=main_assistant
  session=cron:c0b8735a-...:run:aaeb2670-6e9d-4c41-9434-0a0a3cc0614a
  stream=lifecycle phase=start

16:41:46 → event agent run=aaeb2670…614a
  stream=lifecycle aseq=439 phase=end aborted=false
```

*Agent called image_generate, background task started:*
```
Assistant output: "已提交日落图像生成任务（ID: 4c824733）。任务在后台处理中…
  完成后将由 completion agent 在此会话中回传结果。当前状态：处理中。"

→ event task seq=per-client (×4 task events — background task lifecycle)
```

*Model-fetch calls (3 total — cron agent + wake agents):*
```
16:41:28 [model-fetch] start provider=deepseek model=deepseek-v4-pro
  → 200 OK, 365ms                              ← cron agent primary run

16:41:36 [model-fetch] start provider=deepseek model=deepseek-v4-pro  
  → 200 OK, 346ms                              ← async completion wake #1

16:41:39 [model-fetch] start provider=deepseek model=deepseek-v4-pro
  → 200 OK, 353ms                              ← async completion wake #2
```

*Message processed — wake attempted delivery:*
```
message processed: channel=cron sessionKey=agent:main_assistant:cron:c0b8735a-...:run:aaeb2670-...
  outcome=error duration=18229ms
  error="Channel is required when multiple channels are configured: qqbot, feishu."
```

The delivery error is expected — this is an **isolated** session without a channel configured. The wake agent itself ran successfully (model-fetch confirmed), attempted delivery, and could not find a channel. This is the correct behavior; in production, a cron job with a configured delivery channel would receive the completion message.

**Step 4: Session store — bootstrapContextRunKind persisted**
```
Key: agent:main_assistant:cron:c0b8735a-d64c-4373-bcdd-9fa908790196
  bootstrapContextRunKind: cron          ← ✅ persisted on base cron key
  modelProvider: deepseek                ← ✅ cron-configured model
  model: deepseek-v4-pro                 ← ✅ cron-configured model
```

**Step 5: Run-key fallback proof (on live session store)**
```
Run key lookup:  agent:main_assistant:cron:c0b8735a-...:run:run-deadbeef
  → NOT in store  ✅  (expected — run keys never persisted)

Base key lookup: agent:main_assistant:cron:c0b8735a-...
```

target.title: feat: sleep tool — pause execution without burning tokens
target.body:
## Problem

When an agent needs to wait for an external process to complete (background tasks, API rate limits, deployment pipelines, long-running builds), it currently has two bad options:

1. **Poll in a loop** — burn tokens on repeated tool calls checking status every few seconds. The agent becomes noisy, the turn stays open, and the user sees spam. We hit this hard with Planclave polling — 20+ poll calls burning tokens while waiting for a multi-agent planning cycle to finish.

2. **Use cron wake events as a workaround** — schedule a one-shot cron job to fire a wake event after N seconds. This works but is awkward: it creates disposable jobs, fragments turn context (wake comes back as a system event, not a continuation), and requires the agent to reconstruct its state.

Neither option is what users actually want: "wait 5 minutes, then continue where I left off."

## Proposal

Add a `sleep` tool that allows the agent to suspend the current turn and resume it after a specified delay.

### API

```
sleep({ seconds: 300, resumeMessage?: "Check Planclave session status" })
```

### Behavior

1. Agent calls `sleep({ seconds: N })`
2. Gateway **immediately ends the current turn** (no token burn during wait)
3. Gateway schedules an internal wake event after N seconds
4. When the timer fires, the gateway injects a system event and resumes the agent loop in the same session
5. Agent picks up with full turn context intact and can continue execution

### Key Requirements

- **Hard cap on duration** — configurable max (suggest 600s default) to prevent abuse
- **No token burn while waiting** — the turn must truly end, not just block
- **Same session, same context** — resume should feel like a continuation, not a new conversation
- **Interruptible** — if the user sends a message during the wait, it should cancel the timer and process the message immediately
- **Fallback** — if Gateway restarts during a sleep, the timer should not survive (fire-and-forget, not durable)

### Implementation Notes

The existing cron infrastructure already supports one-shot `at` schedules and wake events. The new piece is:

1. A thin wrapper tool that creates a one-shot wake event and signals the gateway to end the turn cleanly
2. A `resume_turn` primitive in the gateway that injects a wake event and re-enters the agent loop without user input
3. The `end_turn` signal — the tool response needs to tell the gateway "close this turn, I'll be back"

The `endTurn` concept already exists in the talk-mode session controller. The agent loop already handles system events and cron wake events. Most of the plumbing is there.

### Use Cases

- **Polling long-running processes** — Planclave cycles, CI builds, deployments, background tasks
- **Rate limit cooldowns** — "I got a 429, wait 60s then retry"
- **Awaiting external state changes** — "wait for the file to appear on the server"
- **Patient monitoring** — heartbeat-style checks where the agent doesn't need to respond to the user between polls

### Current Workarounds and Their Problems

- **Poll in a loop** — Burns tokens, spams output, turns feel slow
- **Cron wake event** — Fragmented context, disposable job creation, awkward
- **Sub-agent monitoring** — Overkill for simple waits, extra complexity
- **sessions_yield** — Only works for spawned sub-agents, not self-pauses

### Related

- #50996 (closed) — Interruptible tool calls (related pain point, different solution)

## Environment

- OpenClaw (latest)
- Windows, macOS, Linux
- All channels (webchat, Discord, Telegram, etc.)

Fixes an issue where Feishu WebSocket users who explicitly configure `channels.feishu.encryptKey` as a SecretRef would have that configured key ignored during runtime secret resolution, even though the same field worked when configured as a plain string.

target.title: fix(web-shared): treat exact-limit response reads as complete
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readResponseText` in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.ts` marks a bounded streamed read as truncated when `bytesRead >= maxBytes`, even when the response body is exactly `maxBytes` bytes. This produces a false `truncated: true` for exact-size responses, which `web_fetch` surfaces as a user-visible "response body truncated" warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

The original code at line 275:

```ts
if (truncated || bytesRead >= maxBytes) {
  truncated = true;
  break;
}
```

When a chunk fills `maxBytes` exactly (e.g. 11 bytes in two chunks "hello" + " world"), the overflow guard on line 262 (`bytesRead + chunk.byteLength > maxBytes`) does not fire, so we reach line 275 with `bytesRead === maxBytes` and `truncated === false`. The `>=` check unconditionally marks this as truncated.

Fix: when `truncated` is already true (trimmed overflow chunk), break immediately. When `bytesRead` hits the limit without overflow, read one more chunk from the stream to confirm whether data was actually omitted.

## Evidence

Two new regression tests in `src/agents/tools/web-shared.test.ts`:

1. **Exact-limit read is NOT truncated**: `["hello", " world"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: false, bytesRead: 11 }`, no reader cancellation
2. **More data after exact limit IS truncated**: `["hello", " world", "more data"]` with `maxBytes: 11` → `{ text: "hello world", truncated: true, bytesRead: 11 }`, reader cancelled

```
✓ does not mark an exact-limit read as truncated
✓ marks as truncated when the next chunk confirms more data after exact limit
```

All 26 tests across all web-shared test suites pass.

## Merge Risk

Low — one targeted change to the boundary condition in the streaming read loop. The overflow-trimming path and the fully-uncapped path are untouched.

target.body:
> **AI-assisted PR.** Implemented with the GitHub Copilot CLI (Claude). The author has reviewed and understands all changes; validated locally (targeted Vitest suites, `tsgo` typecheck, oxlint/oxfmt, SDK surface budget) and against a live `*.ghe.com` tenant (see Evidence). ## What Problem This Solves Organizations on a data-residency GitHub Enterprise tenant (a `*.ghe.com` host such as `your-org.ghe.com`) could not use GitHub Copilot with OpenClaw. Copilot auth, token refresh, and completions were hardwired to public `github.com` / `api.github.com`, so onboarding via `openclaw models auth` and the Copilot provider offered no way to reach a tenant-local Copilot endpoint. Enterprise users were effectively locked out of the Copilot provider. ## Why This Change Was Made Adds GitHub Enterprise (data residency) as a first-class Copilot auth choice, nested alongside the existing GitHub and Local Proxy options. Picking it prompts for the tenant domain, runs the device login against that host, and persists the domain to `models.providers.github-copilot.params.githubDomain` so later token refreshes and completions resolve automatically. Domain resolution follows `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` env > config > `github.com`. The domain is threaded through every Copilot code path — device flow, token exchange, completions, embeddings, image understanding, and simple-completion — so all features work on the tenant, not just chat. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged (no config is written for the default host). No config schema change (uses free-form provider params). **Security (fail-closed by design):** the host allowlist is locked to `github.com` and `*.ghe.com` tenants only — any other value (typo or injected `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN`/config) falls back to `github.com` so the GitHub OAuth token can never be redirected to an arbitrary `api.`. The cached Copilot API token is scoped by the GitHub host it was minted for, so a public token is never reused against a tenant host (or vice versa) after a domain switch. **Domain-switch re-authentication:** onboarding no longer reuses a stored Copilot token when the selected domain differs from the one the token was minted under. Any switch (public `github.com` ↔ a `*.ghe.com` tenant, or one tenant to another) forces a fresh device login so the persisted `githubDomain` always matches a tenant-scoped token; re-running login for the *same* domain still offers to reuse the current token. Switching back to public `github.com` clears the persisted `githubDomain` so config returns to the default (no config == `github.com`). This closes the gap where declining re-login could write a tenant domain against an unverified public token. ## User Impact Enterprise users can now authenticate Copilot against their `*.ghe.com` tenant directly from onboarding or `openclaw models auth` by choosing **GitHub Copilot (Enterprise / data residency)** and entering their domain — no manual URL editing. Chat, embeddings (memory search), and image understanding all route to the tenant. `COPILOT_GITHUB_DOMAIN` enables fully headless/CI setups. Non-enterprise users see no change. ## Scope & Related Work Closes #102219. This PR extends the **existing bundled `github-copilot` provider** with data-residency domain support for the auth, token-exchange, and completions paths it already ships. It does **not** add a new provider, a new model catalog, or a config-schema change (it uses free-form provider params). Related: #96988 ("GHE.com Model Integration"), which was closed NOT_PLANNED and routed to ClawHub/plugin scope. That issue asked for a broader/new GHE model integration; this change is deliberately narrower: it makes the provider OpenClaw already bundles honor an allowlisted, fail-closed `*.ghe.com` tenant host so enterprise users are not locked out, without introducing new SDK provider surface. Public `github.com` behavior is unchanged. **AI-assisted:** developed and validated with AI coding agents (Copilot, Claude) under human direction; all changes human-reviewed, with live tenant validation run by the author. ## Evidence Live validation against a real data-residency GHE tenant (domain/token redacted): ### [P1] GHE Login, Token Refresh & Completion — Redacted Evidence 1. ## Summary

- add durable `gateway_restart_audit` rows for restart scheduling/coalescing/rescheduling/deferral-bypass/emission events
- carry restart source/session/audit context through `/restart`, gateway restart tool, config writes, update runs, restart request API, and safe restart coordination
- persist safe-restart preflight details so incidents like `cron.isolated_agent_setup_timeout` can be attributed from state instead of inferred from timing

## What Problem This Solves

Gateway restart forensics currently loses the initiating reason/source for internal safe restart requests. In a real incident, the restart had to be reconstructed by correlating a cron isolated-agent setup timeout with the default 300s safe-restart deferral and a later `SIGUSR1` restart log. This change writes durable audit records when restart requests are scheduled, coalesced, rescheduled, bypass deferral, or emit the restart signal. target.title: feat(tools/write): add append mode for agent writes
target.body:
## Summary

Revives and rebases the closed append-mode work from #75549 for the canonical data-loss issue #40001.

The `write` tool currently overwrites existing files. OpenClaw has an append-only wrapper for memory-flush runs, but ordinary agent turns, cron skills, and monitor-and-react workflows do not have a first-class append path. This PR adds a backwards-compatible optional `append: true` parameter to `write` so agents can append without synthesizing a read-concatenate-overwrite sequence.

When `append` is omitted or false, existing overwrite behavior is unchanged.

## What changed

- Adds optional `append?: boolean` handling for host/workspace and sandbox write operations.
- Preserves existing workspace/root guard behavior.
- Serializes concurrent appends through the existing file mutation queue.
- Preserves validation behavior for blank paths and invalid content.
- Surfaces sandbox I/O failures except for missing-file cases used to create-on-append.
- Honors aborted append calls before entering the mutation queue.
- Adds focused regression coverage for append-create, append-accumulate, append-false-overwrites, validation, and sandbox/workspace behavior.

## Validation

Run in an isolated checkout on current `origin/main`:

- `corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`
- `corepack pnpm exec vitest run src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.read.host-tilde-expansion.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts src/agents/pi-tools.params.test.ts`
  - passed: `10 files / 170 tests`
- `git diff --check`
- `corepack pnpm lint:core`
  - passed: `0 warnings / 0 errors`

## Notes

This PR intentionally keeps the API small and backwards-compatible. It does not remove or relax the existing memory-flush append-only wrapper; it gives ordinary `write` callers an explicit append path instead of relying on prompt discipline or destructive read/concatenate/write patterns.

Fixes #40001.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** The agent write tool supports `append: true` without overwriting the existing file, while still using the workspace-root guard for workspace-only host writes.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw source checkout on Linux using the actual `createHostWorkspaceWriteTool` implementation against a temporary workspace on the real filesystem.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran a `node --import tsx` terminal smoke that created the host workspace write tool, wrote `first line`, reran the same write tool with `append: true` for `second line`, then read the resulting file.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture from the smoke:

  ```text
  workspace: $TMPDIR/openclaw-write-append-proof-.../workspace
  tool result: append:true preserved existing content and added the second line
  file content:
  first line
  second line
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** The final file retained the original content and appended the new content in order; the append path did not truncate or replace the file.
- **What was not tested:** No live Gateway session was exercised; validation used the real tool implementation in an isolated local checkout plus targeted regression/type checks.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101967: The loopback MCP bridge resolved tools without the auth profile store, so OAuth-only provider tools (e.g. xAI `x_search`/`code_execution`) never registered for CLI-backend (claude-cli) sessions.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `authProfileStore` to `McpLoopbackScopeParams` and threaded it through `resolveGatewayScopedTools`, matching the pattern used by other tool resolution paths. The fix touches three call sites:

- **`mcp-http.runtime.ts`** — accept `authProfileStore` in the loopback scope params
- **`tool-resolution.ts`** — pipe `authProfileStore` through `resolveGatewayScopedTools`
- **`prepare.ts`** — pass the loaded `authStore` when resolving loopback tools

## Why This Is Better Than #101982

PR #101982 applies the same plumbing fix but adds **no regression test**. This PR includes a focused regression test in `mcp-http.test.ts` that verifies `authProfileStore` is passed through to `resolveGatewayScopedTools` when `resolveMcpLoopbackScopedTools` is called.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Vertex AI users who configure their project with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` would have Vertex project detection treat the project as missing, even though the Google OAuth path already accepts that env name.

## Why This Change Was Made

This aligns the Vertex runtime project resolver, ADC credential-marker eligibility, pre-runtime auth evidence, operator-facing provider env metadata, and the published `@openclaw/ai` built-in Vertex surface with the existing Google OAuth project env support. Without updating the auth evidence contract, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`-only ADC setups could still be classified as unauthenticated before the Vertex transport path runs.

The change keeps the existing env behavior intact for `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GCLOUD_PROJECT`, and explicit project options, and does not change credential formats, config schema, migrations, provider selection, or default model routing.

## User Impact

Operators can use `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` for Google Vertex AI without duplicating the same value into `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `GCLOUD_PROJECT`. Existing Vertex setups using the older env names continue to work.
