target.title: feat: add sessions_search transcript search
target.body:
Closes #100978

AI-assisted: yes (Codex)

## What Problem This Solves

Agents currently cannot search their own prior session transcripts when they remember a topic, decision, identifier, or phrase but do not know the exact session key or history page. That makes long-running work harder to resume and forces agents to list sessions manually, then page through histories one by one.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a first-class `sessions_search` agent tool backed by a new Gateway method, `sessions.search`, and a per-agent SQLite FTS5 transcript index. The design keeps the new capability inside the existing session-tool privacy model: agents can only search sessions they could already inspect with `sessions_history`, and no new config surface or cross-agent policy is introduced.

Technical shape:

- Agent tool surface: `sessions_search` accepts `{ query, sessionKey?, limit? }`. When `sessionKey` is omitted, the tool first calls `sessions.list` and filters rows through the same effective `tools.sessions.visibility` and agent-to-agent rules used by history/list tooling. When `sessionKey` is present, it resolves and checks the explicit target before search.
- Gateway API: `sessions.search` accepts `query`, optional `sessionKey`/`sessionKeys`, optional `agentId`, and optional `limit`. It returns bounded hits with `sessionKey`, `sessionId`, `agentId`, `seq`, `role`, `snippet`, and optional timestamp/message id so callers can follow up with `sessions_history`.
- Storage/indexing: the per-agent SQLite DB now owns `session_transcript_search_sources` plus an FTS5 virtual table. Search reconciles each targeted transcript by stat metadata (`mtime`, `size`, canonical session key) before querying, so unchanged transcripts are reused and changed transcripts are reindexed.
- Stale-row protection: replacing a session key's transcript path purges old FTS/source rows for that key before inserting the new rows, preventing search from returning snippets that current `sessions_history` would no longer show.
- Indexed content boundary: only user/assistant visible transcript text is indexed. The index strips inline directive tags, applies the existing tool-payload redaction helper, truncates large message text before indexing, and excludes tool/system/internal records.
- Query behavior: FTS queries quote whitespace-delimited terms for SQLite FTS5 `MATCH`, rank by `bm25`, and use `snippet(...)` for compact excerpts. A LIKE fallback handles FTS parser failures without widening the session scope.
- Generated/client surfaces: Gateway protocol schemas/types are exported, native Swift protocol models are regenerated, and tool display metadata plus the shared tool-display snapshot are updated.

Non-goals and boundaries:

- No new `openclaw.json` option or environment variable.
- No background watcher or persistent worker; the index is reconciled when search targets are requested.
- No cross-plugin policy in core; visibility remains delegated to the existing session-tool helpers.

## User Impact

Agents can now search visible session transcripts by phrase and get concise, redacted snippets with enough provenance to open the exact session history afterward. Users get better recall across long-running work without broadening access beyond existing session visibility rules.

## Evidence

Local validation after CI fixes:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server.sessions.store-rpc.test.ts src/agents/tools/sessions-search-tool.test.ts` - passed 2 shards, 2 files, 8 tests.

- `node scripts/run-oxlint-shards.mjs --threads=8` - passed.
- `node --import tsx scripts/tool-display.ts --check` - passed.
- `pnpm check:architecture` - passed.
- `pnpm protocol:check` - passed after committing regenerated Swift protocol models.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo` - passed.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` - clean after the CI-fix commit.

Redacted runtime proof added after ClawSweeper review:

- `node --import tsx .artifacts/proof/sessions-search-proof.mjs` - passed on Node v24.14.1 against HEAD `76409e64a2ed` using an isolated temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`; synthetic transcript only, no secrets.

## Summary

Draft review PR for the CLI catalog effort described in the RFC: https://github.com/giodl73-repo/rfcs/blob/codex/cli-catalog-overlay-rfc/rfcs/0010-cli-catalog-overlay.md

- audit, test-matrix, and operator summary views

target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: fix: stabilize room-event prompt cache mode
target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes avoidable prompt-cache churn when Discord/channel room events with `visibleReplies: automatic` interleave with normal session turns.

The redacted live symptom was same-session turns alternating between warm provider cache prefixes and near-cold prefixes even though the configured visible-reply policy was stable.

## What Changed

Strict room-event delivery remains unchanged: non-internal room events still use `message_tool_only` for actual visible delivery and `forceMessageTool`.

This PR separates the prompt-facing delivery mode from the effective delivery mode, then forwards the prompt-facing mode through direct, queued, Codex app-server, Codex dynamic-tool construction, embedded tool-construction, and memory/flush runner paths. System-prompt construction and cache-visible tool inventory can use the session-stable prompt mode while actual room-event output remains message-tool-only.

The queue delivery-context key also includes the prompt-facing mode, so collect batching does not merge turns whose prompt contracts differ.

The latest head also preserves the owner-only Gateway tool boundary:
- direct owner turns keep owner-only core tools such as `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`
- explicit non-owner turns still do not receive those tools
- ambient `room_event` turns use the same safe owner-only core-tool inventory, including owner-sent room events, so room-event cache prefixes do not flip by sender

## User Impact

Room-event turns preserve a stable prompt/cache contract without relaxing message-tool-only delivery or widening non-owner access to owner-only Gateway tools.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR by Codex. Private identifiers are redacted.

Original redacted live trace evidence from #102175:
- Same agent/session family, same provider/model family, repeated turns within one minute.
- Prompt input sizes around `37k-46.5k` tokens alternated with cached prefixes of `0`, `2k`, `9.9k`, and `47.6k` tokens.
- The regression correlated with room-event turns where runtime metadata reported `visible_reply_contract: message_tool_only` even though resolved config used `messages.visibleReplies: automatic`.
- Source inspection on current `main` showed strict room-event effective delivery still forcing `message_tool_only`, while cache-sensitive system-prompt sections derive prompt directives from the mode passed into prompt construction.

Diagnostic redacted provider traces also found an owner/non-owner room-event inventory invalidator before the final boundary-preserving fix:
- Same-session traces differed between `tools=47` and `tools=44`.
- The three missing tools were `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes`.
- Gateway logs for the cold-prefix turn showed: `[agents/tool-policy] tool policy removed 3 tool(s) via gateway sender owner-only tools.deny: cron, gateway, nodes`.
- Current head avoids that sender flip for ambient room events by using the safe room-event inventory consistently, while keeping explicit non-owner inventories filtered.

Current-head live smoke evidence after installing this branch locally:
- Same channel/session class retested after the prompt-mode follow-up.
- Provider dashboard showed cached prefixes reaching approximately `49k-52k` tokens on a `~51k-55k` context, instead of the prior `~40k` ceiling observed on the same path.
- The local status command reported `0 new` prompt-cache tokens for those warm checks.

Current-head validation:
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts --testNamePattern "prompt-facing delivery mode|message-tool-only source replies|registered schema override"` — passed, 3 tests.
- `pnpm vitest run extensions/codex/src/app-server/dynamic-tool-build.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/run-attempt.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.spawn-workspace.context-engine.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner-utils.test.ts --testNamePattern "prompt-facing delivery mode|developer reply instructions|source reply delivery mode|owner-only tool authorization|embedded tool construction|prompt cache affinity|message-tool-only source replies|registered schema override"` — passed, 5 files, 13 tests.

- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/agent-tools-agent-config.test.ts src/agents/agent-tools.create-openclaw-coding-tools.test.ts --testNamePattern "keeps core tools for owner WebChat while restricting non-owners|owner-only core tool|room events"` — passed, 4 tests.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm build` — passed.

Current-head test coverage specifically proves:
- queued followups forward `promptSourceReplyDeliveryMode`
- memory/flush embedded runs forward `promptSourceReplyDeliveryMode`
- Codex developer instructions use the prompt-facing delivery mode
- Codex dynamic-tool construction uses the prompt-facing delivery mode for cache-visible tool inventory
- embedded tool construction uses the prompt-facing delivery mode for cache-visible inventory

target.title: fix(memory-wiki): salvage human Notes before pruning imported source pages
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #102230 — when `pruneImportedSourceEntries` removes a page whose syncKey
legitimately left `activeKeys`, it force-deletes the page file including the
human-authored `## Notes` block with no salvage, archive, or tombstone.

## Root Cause

`pruneImportedSourceEntries` calls `fs.rm` with no read of the page content
and no check for the human Notes block. Normal syncs protect Notes via
`preserveHumanNotesBlock`, but the prune path bypasses preservation entirely.

## Fix

Before removing the page, read it and extract the human Notes block (only after
`## Content` fence — mirrors `afterSourceContentFence` in markdown.ts). If
present, write to `.salvage/<page>.notes.md`. If salvage write fails, keep the
page so Notes are not lost.

## Evidence

### End-to-End Proof — production function

```
node --import tsx -e 'import { pruneImportedSourceEntries }...'

BEFORE: page exists, salvage dir: no

AFTER prune (1 pages): page deleted, salvage:
<!-- openclaw:human:start -->
real annotations survive
<!-- openclaw:human:end -->
source marker NOT salvaged: OK
```

### Regression Tests

5 tests in `extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync-state.test.ts`:
- salvages human Notes before pruning
- does not create salvage files for pages without human Notes
- prunes pages even when the page file is already missing
- does not salvage marker comments inside source content as Notes
- keeps the page when salvage write fails

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-wiki/src/source-sync-state.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)  Tests  9 passed (9)
```

### Autoreview

```
python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude
autoreview clean: no accepted/actionable findings reported
overall: patch is correct (0.95)
```

## Change Type / Scope / Security Impact

- **Change type**: `fix` — data-loss bug: prune silently destroys human Notes
- **Scope**: memory-wiki plugin only (`extensions/memory-wiki/src/`)
- **Security**: No new permissions, secrets, or network calls. Writes to
  `.salvage/` under vault root with sanitized filenames. Fails-safe: if
  salvage write fails, the page is kept.

- [x] oxfmt + oxlint pass
- [x] git diff --check pass
- [x] autoreview clean

target.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin even after the locally installed Codex.app bundle was updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

That is how a request could ask for Codex Computer Use while the runtime silently lacked a working Computer Use bridge or fell back to other automation without making the failure inspectable.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a real copied cache entry that Codex can discover and removing stale cached versions
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and opt-in narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children when `computerUse.autoRepair` is true
- opt-in periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes when `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` is true, using the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence and the same live-probe path
- fail-closed setup behavior by default while keeping browser/DOM fallback available when explicitly requested outside the Computer Use setup path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckEnabled`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `fallbackOnFailure`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache even after Codex.app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, did not reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed Codex.app bundle, and did not prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

## Evidence

Post-rebase on current `origin/main` (`45d0970a7d`) with PR head `af1c8f0264cf80ce30f034233d6304316b8b3116`, I verified the patch locally with targeted unit coverage, command/doctor coverage, docs-map proof, TypeScript test checks, an exact-head live Codex.app Computer Use proof, and a merge-result tree check:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- `node scripts/generate-docs-map.mjs --check` — `docs/docs_map.md` is up to date
- `node scripts/test-extension.mjs codex extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-cache.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-health.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use-leases.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/config.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/request.test.ts extensions/codex/src/app-server/attempt-startup.test.ts extensions/codex/src/commands.test.ts` — 8 files, 301 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts src/commands/doctor/shared/codex-route-warnings.test.ts` — 1 file, 112 tests passed
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo`
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo`
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor origin/main HEAD` — passed; `origin/main` is an ancestor of the exact PR head

target.title: Interactive parity with the Codex runtime: ask-user-question · plan mode · goal mode
target.body:
> **The agent that asks, plans, and pursues.** This PR gives every OpenClaw session the three interactive primitives Codex-native users already have: the agent can ask structured questions (options + "(Recommended)" + free-text "Other", answerable from any surface), enter a real plan mode (read-only enforcement, a live plan panel, approve-to-execute), and pursue a long-running goal unattended behind a safety-gated continuation driver with a visible "Pursuing goal" chip.

Master hub: #102260 (architecture diagrams, the full test map, and the follow-up roadmap live there).

![Interactive parity demo: mode selector → plan mode with a live checklist in the right sidebar → inline approval → agent question answered inline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/parity-demo.gif)

*The full flow — plan mode, the live plan pane, inline approval, and an inline agent question. A [30s narrated walkthrough](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) covers goal mode too.*

## Why this shape
The primitives were **already merged** (`update_plan` experimental, goal state tools, a codex user-input bridge, `stream:plan` events, exec-approval UI, Telegram/Slack buttons) — this PR is the completion layer, and every feature rides an existing choke point rather than inventing a parallel system. One branch, **take-apart commit groups** (reviewable and revertable independently; happy to split into stacked PRs on request) — the three feature groups, then a Control-UI pass bringing the surface to Codex-Desktop parity (inline composer cards, right-sidebar plan, mode selector, goal modal):

| Commits | Group | Delivers |
|---|---|---|
| 1–11 | **Question infra** | `ask_user_question` tool · global QuestionManager (exec-approval pattern) · `question.list/resolve` + events · Control-UI card · Telegram/Slack buttons + proactive push · `/answer` · restart expiry-sweep · codex-bridge convergence (structured vs free-text race) |
| 12–21 | **Plan mode** | plan-state slot + `enter/exit_plan_mode` · read-only gate at the single before-tool-call choke point · `update_plan` promoted default-on · live plan panel · `/plan` commands + structured channel summaries · exit-plan approval rides the question infra |
| 22–27 | **Goal mode** | continuation driver (debounced, 4-gated, never self-re-arms) · durable no-progress ceiling · `/goal set/edit/pause/resume/stop --budget` · "Pursuing goal" pill + edit modal · single-source `goal.updated` · behind `tools.experimental.goalDriver` |
| 28–36 | **Control-UI parity pass** | composer goal-pill Lit-race fix · questions & plan-approval as **inline composer cards** (modals retired) · active plan **docked in the right sidebar** · **mode selector** (off/plan/goal, mutually exclusive) by the gear · goal-editor **modal** with card chrome · whole-program type + lint clean |

## What each feature does

### 1 · Structured questions
`ask_user_question` (1-3 questions, 2-4 options, first recommended, auto-"Other") parks the *tool* on a global-manager promise — the exec-approval pattern — so the answer can come from anywhere: an **inline card in the chat composer** (Codex-Desktop style, not a page-locking modal), Telegram inline buttons or Slack Block Kit (pushed proactively to the turn-source chat, deduped), or `/answer <n|text>` on any channel. Ask on Telegram, answer in the browser. No default timeout (humans sleep); a gateway restart expires pending questions loudly (`question.expired`) instead of hanging. Codex-runtime sessions converge: their `request_user_input` (already held open as a JSON-RPC request) now renders the same card, racing the structured answer against the legacy next-free-text path.

![The agent's question rendered inline in the composer: numbered options, a Recommended chip, an "Other" free-text option, with 1-of-N paging](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/question-inline.png)

### 2 · Plan mode
The **mode selector by the gear** (or `/plan` / `enter_plan_mode`) puts the session in a read-only collaboration mode enforced as a **core policy at the one choke point every tool execution funnels through** — built-ins incl. exec and subagent spawn, plugin/MCP-backed, catalog, code-mode, client tools. The agent researches and maintains a live checklist (`update_plan`, promoted from experimental with a kill-switch) that ticks in real time in the **right-sidebar plan pane** (always viewable, full rendered plan; a compact chip stays inline); `exit_plan_mode` persists the plan to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/plans/` and asks for approval as an **inline composer card** (one pipeline for all human-in-the-loop moments); reject-with-feedback loops the agent back into planning. The mode selector keeps plan and goal mutually exclusive.

![Plan mode: the live checklist docked in the right sidebar with completed steps struck through, and the inline "Implement this plan?" approval card in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-sidebar.png)

![The exit-plan approval as an inline composer card — Approve or Revise-with-feedback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/plan-approval-inline.png)

### 3 · Goal mode
`/goal set "<objective>" --budget <n>` (or the chip dialog) and walk away. The driver mirrors the Codex goal extension's idle-continuation semantics, adapted honestly to OpenClaw's architecture (no idle event exists — a spike proved the safe shape first): a debounced scheduler armed **only** by turn-completion, firing **only** when four gates pass (goal active · no active run · queue empty · no-progress ceiling not hit), via the cron system-event path + a heartbeat wake. **After a fire it never self-re-arms** — cadence is structurally bounded, no tight loop. Ceiling hit → auto-pause. Budget hit → disarm. The model can only mark `complete|blocked` (host-only pause, mirroring Codex).

![The goal editor modal — objective, token budget, and Save, with the "Pursuing goal" pill live in the composer](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/c57fe74c64e15e1de7a76e742598904ff207c849/docs/assets/interactive-parity/goal-editor.png)

## Security
- **Questions**: human-in-the-loop by construction — no new privilege; answers are typed user input on existing paths; resolution needs the same scopes as approval resolution; proactive push only targets the question's own turn-source chat.
- **Plan gate**: fail-closed at the single choke point, with an **in-PR adversarial suite**: exec, MCP tool, plugin tool, and subagent-spawn are each proven vetoed through the real hook.
- **Goal driver**: a driver-continued turn has exactly the privileges of a user turn — the in-PR safety test raises an exec approval *during* a driver-continued turn and it blocks normally. Layered brakes: debounce+jitter · 4 gates · durable ceiling · budget states · experimental flag (default off).

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** agents couldn't ask, couldn't plan reviewably, couldn't pursue; codex `request_user_input` degraded to plain text; `update_plan` events rendered as a bare text line.
**Evidence (full gate on the final tip, run and read by the submitting orchestrator):** 9 backend suites in one run (question manager/wire-contract integration/tool/forwarder/sweep/`/answer` · plan state machine + **adversarial bypass matrix** + approval wire-contract · goal driver loop-safety + integration probe + wiring/safety + commands + durability) — all green; `tsgo` core + test 0; UI suites 781/784 (the 3 = the long-documented `terminal-panel` fixture flake, failing identically on pristine `main` — verified); `ui:i18n:check` clean; `ui:build` 0; **full type-aware `pnpm lint` 0**. The wire-contract integration tests land IN this PR: client↔gateway param drift fails CI here, not in production.

*▶ [Full 30s narrated walkthrough (mp4)](https://github.com/100yenadmin/openclaw/releases/download/interactive-parity-media-v1/parity-demo.mp4) — questions, plan mode, the sidebar plan, inline approval, and goal mode running unattended.*

## Dependency note
No new dependencies; no lockfile change. Plan-mode semantics derive from a 156-case parity-hardened prior implementation; goal-driver semantics mirror `codex-rs/ext/goal` for cross-runtime consistency. Codex plan/goal wire bridges are documented in-code as follow-up seams (hub roadmap) — no speculative plumbing.

target.title: Add Claw status and remove lifecycle
target.body:
## Summary

Final OpenClaw PR in the current Claws stack. This adds the first supported lifecycle management commands over the state produced by the mutating apply PRs:

- `claws status [claw] --json` reports persisted Claw apply records, plugin artifact refs, and workspace file refs
- `claws remove <claw> --dry-run --json` previews removal without deleting files or refs
- `claws remove <claw> --yes --json` removes persisted Claw refs and deletes unchanged Claw-managed workspace files
- user-modified, oversized, missing, or already-deleted workspace files are retained or treated as stale cleanup instead of being deleted unsafely
- workspace removal preflights all refs before deleting any file, revalidates the managed hash immediately before unlinking, and keeps failed refs visible in status on partial cleanup errors
- artifact refs are removed as Claw provenance only; this does not uninstall plugin packages

## Stack

- RFC: openclaw/rfcs#27
- Validation/dry-run foundation: #101328
- Artifact provenance refs: #101755
- Workspace/persona files apply: #101973
- Plugin artifact installers + warning provenance: #102228
- This PR: Claw status/remove lifecycle

## Behavior Notes

This intentionally stops short of update, rollback, automation/crons, skill/MCP/connectors installers, and ClawHub discovery. It gives users an end-to-end supported lifecycle for the state that the current stack can already create: apply, inspect persisted state, preview removal, remove Claw-owned metadata, and clean unchanged managed workspace files.

`claws remove` does not ref-count-lock or uninstall plugins. It removes Claw refs so future plugin uninstall warnings no longer include the removed Claw.

## Real Behavior Proof

The E2E suite now runs a full real CLI lifecycle using `node --import tsx src/entry.ts`:

1. apply a local plugin Claw with `--yes --workspace --json`
2. verify `claws status <id> --json` reports artifact and workspace refs
3. verify `claws remove <id> --dry-run --json` previews workspace deletion without deleting the file
4. run `claws remove <id> --yes --json`
5. verify the managed workspace file is deleted
6. verify final `claws status <id> --json` is empty

## Validation

Run on WSL worktree `/root/src/openclaw-claws-pr6-lifecycle` at head `49eb30ad775269f7ad48e7817a1cc4c45acb70c6`:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/claws/artifact-installers.test.ts src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle-state.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/cli/plugins-cli.uninstall.test.ts src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts src/cli/program/command-registry.test.ts src/cli/program/root-command-descriptions.test.ts
```

Result: passed 3 Vitest shards: unit 84 tests, CLI 42 tests, lifecycle E2E 5 tests.

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs
```

Result: passed.

```text
pnpm exec tsgo --noEmit --pretty false
```

Result: still blocked only by existing unrelated baseline:

```text
src/secrets/config-io.ts(12,17): error TS4058: Return type of exported function has or is using name 'configWritePostCommitRollback' from external module "/root/src/openclaw-claws-pr6-lifecycle/src/config/io" but cannot be named.
```

```text
codex review -c model=gpt-5.5 --base origin/user/giodl/claws-pr5-installers
```

target.title: fix(security): ignore string-literal contents in code-safety env/exfil rules (#82469)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The plugin `code_safety` scanner raises **critical `env-harvesting`** (and `potential-exfiltration`) false positives on ordinary plugin and test files. `stripCommentsForHeuristics` masks comments but **keeps string-literal contents**, so a network-send token (`fetch(`, `.post(`, `http.request(`) that appears only *inside a string* — e.g. `fetch(` in an `it("...")` description, or in static backtick-template text — counts as rule context. Combined with a legitimate `process.env` / `readFile` access, that yields a critical credential-harvesting finding on code that never makes a network call. (`src/skills/security/scanner.ts`; issue #82469.)

Verified against current `main` — both quoting styles false-positive:

```
TRUE main:  process.env + fetch( inside "double-quoted" string   => critical:env-harvesting   (false positive)
TRUE main:  process.env + fetch( inside static `backtick` text   => critical:env-harvesting   (false positive)
```

## Why This Change Was Made

This supersedes the auto-closed **#82535**. That PR first tried excluding `*.test.ts` from the scan — which the ClawSweeper review flagged as `merge-risk: security-boundary` because it reduces scan coverage. I reworked it to a root-cause fix; ClawSweeper's review then said *"the root-cause direction is better than excluding test files"* but raised one `[medium]` finding: static backtick-template text was still unmasked. #82535 was then closed by a stale-PR sweep keyed on its original May open date (not on merit). This PR is the completed root-cause fix that closes the backtick gap.

Approach: an opt-in `ignoreStringLiterals` on the two source rules that hunt for **code constructs** (`env-harvesting`, `potential-exfiltration`). They now evaluate against a source with string-literal contents blanked (`maskStringLiteralContents`). Single/double-quoted contents are fully blanked; backtick templates blank only their **static text** and keep `${...}` interpolation bodies (which hold real code), with nested strings tracked so a brace inside `obj["}"]` cannot miscount the boundary. `obfuscated-code` (hex/base64) and `crypto-mining` (`stratum+tcp`) intentionally match string payloads and keep the unmasked source, so their detection is unchanged.

## User Impact

Plugin authors and operators stop getting critical false-positive `env-harvesting` findings from `openclaw doctor` / the code-safety audit for benign `process.env` + string-literal combinations — in production and test files, and for both double-quote and backtick strings — while **every file is still scanned** and real harvesting is still caught. No coverage reduction, so none of the security-boundary risk of the test-file-exclusion approach.

## Evidence

Real `scanSource()` before/after (details in comment below). The only behavior change is the false positives disappearing; every real detection is preserved — including a harvester built from a backtick template with `${process.env.X}`. `oxfmt` clean; scanner suite green (24 tests: 5 new + the existing obfuscated-code/crypto-mining regression guards). Fixes #82469.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Group-channel messages need a generic way to distinguish the runtime message author from the operator/user represented by the agent session. Without source actor attribution, downstream prompts, tools, and memory adapters can only see channel/session context and may conflate another group participant with the operator. This should be solved as a channel contract, not as a deployment-specific memory backend workaround.

## Summary

- Adds a generic `SourceActor` inbound context contract for the runtime identity of the message author.
- Maps Signal sender identity into `SourceActor` without making the contract Signal-specific.
- Types `SourceActorRole` as `operator | participant | self | system | external`.
- Documents `SourceActor` as canonical and the flattened `SourceActor*` fields as scalar mirrors for prompt templates.
- Exports `SourceActorContext` and `SourceActorRole` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-runtime`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 and `codex/signal-mention-facts-context`. Until those land, this PR's diff will include its dependencies.

## Production impact

No behavior change by itself. The change gives prompts, tools, and memory integrations a stable way to distinguish a group participant from the operator/user. Signal direct and group senders are represented as `participant` source actors.

## Evidence

- Channel context tests cover generic `SourceActor` projection and object-to-scalar mirror parity.
- Channel contract helpers now assert `SourceActor` scalar mirrors stay in sync with the canonical structured object.
- Signal mention-gating tests cover Signal sender identity mapping into the generic context.
- Plugin SDK runtime mock tests cover `SourceActor*` parity with production inbound context.
- Focused tests passed:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/channels/inbound-event/context.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/test-helpers/plugin-runtime-mock.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`

- Production TypeScript check passed:

The proof preserves the emitted source-actor shape while replacing all Signal identifiers, group identifiers, participant names, phone numbers, UUIDs, and message bodies with placeholders.

target.title: Support Ultra thinking for the native Codex runtime
target.body:
## Summary

Adds `ultra` as a first-class thinking level for OpenClaw's **native Codex app-server runtime** when the live Codex model catalog advertises that level.

This is intentionally not a generic `ultra -> max` alias. Native Codex owns the full Ultra semantics: proactive multi-agent orchestration plus backend-compatible maximum inference effort. Embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes that do not implement that orchestration do not advertise Ultra.

Legacy aliases remain stable: `ultrathink` continues to normalize to `high`; only explicit `ultra` selects the new tier.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> defines Ultra as a user-facing orchestration level:

- Codex Core selects `MultiAgentMode::Proactive`.
- Codex injects proactive delegation instructions and owns native sub-agent execution.
- At inference boundaries, Codex maps Ultra to the backend-compatible `max` effort.

Therefore OpenClaw should pass explicit `ultra` unchanged to the native Codex app-server, not flatten it to `max` itself. Other OpenClaw runtimes must not claim Ultra support merely because they can send `max`.

## Changes

- Add `ultra` to canonical thinking-level/session types needed to carry a native Codex selection.
- Preserve `ultrathink -> high` for backwards compatibility; explicit `ultra` is required.
- Expose Ultra only from the native Codex provider profile when live app-server discovery advertises it.
- Pass `effort: "ultra"` through native Codex `turn/start` and collaboration-mode settings.
- Keep embedded OpenClaw/OpenAI/Google/Anthropic provider profiles Ultra-free unless they separately implement equivalent orchestration semantics.
- Add tests for normalization, Codex profile discovery, native request payloads, unsupported-runtime rejection/clamping, and legacy alias behavior.
- Update thinking-level documentation with the native-Codex-only scope.

## Evidence

### Official semantics

OpenAI Codex PR <https://github.com/openai/codex/pull/29899> implements Ultra in Codex Core. Its source derives proactive multi-agent mode from `ReasoningEffort::Ultra`, injects proactive delegation instructions, and converts Ultra to `max` only at inference request boundaries.

### Real configured-provider behavior (sanitized)

Codex CLI 0.142.4 was configured with:

```toml
model = "gpt-5.6-sol"
model_reasoning_effort = "ultra"
```

Live model discovery advertised:

```text
gpt-5.6-sol: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
```

A real ephemeral read-only turn completed successfully:

```text
$ codex exec --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only --json \
    'Reply exactly with ULTRA_OK_1424 and nothing else.'
...
item.completed: ULTRA_OK_1424
turn.completed
```

This proves the native Codex 0.142.4 runtime accepts and executes the Ultra selection. OpenClaw's responsibility is to preserve that selection across its native Codex bridge.


### Current-head native app-server bridge proof (sanitized, 2026-07-03)

A current-head OpenClaw bridge proof was run with a disposable app-server home and a non-default entitlement fixture. This is intentionally classified as `PASS_CONTAMINATED_ONLY`; it validates the native app-server entitlement and OpenClaw bridge behavior, not clean-stage default-profile behavior. Production Gateway state and production config were not used.

```text
head: 78fb055d
live model/list target: gpt-5.6-sol
live supportedReasoningEfforts: low, medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra
thread/start: accepted, model=gpt-5.6-sol
turn/start: accepted
captured turn/start.effort: ultra
captured turn/start.collaborationMode.settings.reasoning_effort: ultra
cleanup: copied entitlement fixture absent after run
verdict: APP_SERVER_BRIDGE_ULTRA_OK
```

This directly exercises current-head OpenClaw source constructing a real native Codex app-server `turn/start` request after live discovery advertised Ultra.

### OpenClaw validation

The revised branch passed:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/auto-reply/thinking.test.ts \
  src/llm/model-utils.test.ts \
  src/config/config.schema-regressions.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/provider.test.ts \
  extensions/codex/src/app-server/thread-lifecycle.test.ts

# 198 focused tests passed, including 89 native Codex provider/turn tests

pnpm tsgo:core       # passed
pnpm tsgo:core:test  # passed
```

Additional OpenAI/Anthropic/Google/provider-stream safety suites passed after verifying that non-Codex profiles do not expose Ultra and stale internal Ultra values are handled defensively rather than forwarded as a claimed feature.

## Non-goals

- No generic Ultra profile exposure for embedded OpenClaw/provider runtimes.
- No claim that `max` alone is equivalent to Ultra. Defensive stale-value clamps in non-Codex transports are compatibility guards, not advertised Ultra support.
- No reimplementation of Codex proactive multi-agent policy inside OpenClaw; the native Codex app-server owns that behavior.

target.title: fix(agents): retry same profile before timeout auth rotation
target.body:
## Summary

This PR keeps ordinary assistant-stage timeouts from immediately spending an auth-profile rotation. A first ordinary timeout now gets one bounded retry on the same model/profile; if the retry budget is exhausted, the existing auth-profile rotation path still runs.

The change deliberately does **not** weaken real failover for rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures. Those reasons continue through the existing profile rotation / escalation path rather than being hidden by the timeout retry.

## What Problem This Solves

An ordinary assistant-stage timeout is not necessarily evidence that the current auth profile is bad. Rotating the auth profile on the first ordinary timeout can spend a scarce profile/fallback lane too early and make transient timeout handling look like an auth-profile failure.

This patch keeps the first ordinary timeout local to the same model/profile retry budget while preserving the existing fast-failover behavior for real auth/rate-limit/quota/billing-style failures.

## Why this is not covered by adjacent timeout fixes

Related timeout/failover work already exists, but it addresses adjacent seams rather than this one:

- #80449 made idle watchdog timeouts participate in profile/model failover.
- #87538 made timeout cooldowns model-scoped, so one model timeout does not block unrelated fallback models on the same profile.
- #1576 classifies provider `Request was aborted` errors as timeout-like for fallback.
- #95650 is about compaction retry behavior with backup auth profiles.
- #87122 is about provider overload cooldown semantics.

Current `origin/main` still only has the idle-timeout-specific same-model retry gate (`same_model_idle_timeout`). It does not have an ordinary request-timeout same-profile retry gate before `advanceAuthProfile()`.

## Behavior addressed

Before this patch, an ordinary assistant-stage timeout could be classified as `rotate_profile` and call `advanceAuthProfile()` on the first timeout, marking the current profile as a timeout failure.

After this patch:

- ordinary assistant-stage timeout: retry the same model/profile once first;
- repeated ordinary timeout after the retry budget is exhausted: use the existing auth-profile rotation path;
- rate-limit/auth/quota/billing-style failures: keep existing fast failover behavior;
- compaction/tool-execution timeouts: remain excluded from this assistant-stage retry gate;
- configured fallback is intentionally not a bypass for the first ordinary timeout; the retry budget is one, so fallback/rotation remains available on the next timeout.

## Implementation notes

- Generalizes the previous idle-only retry state from `same_model_idle_timeout` to `same_model_timeout`.
- Keeps the retry budget bounded at one same-profile retry.
- Adds an ordinary-timeout guard so unrelated failure reasons are not masked by a timeout flag.
- Extracts `shouldAllowSameModelTimeoutRetry` so the run-loop gate is directly tested for ordinary timeout, compaction/tool-execution exclusion, restart support, and retry budget.
- Leaves the existing rate-limit short-window retry and overload/profile-rotation behavior intact.

## Session-state blocker addressed in this update

After the proof review, ClawSweeper moved the remaining blocker from proof to `merge-risk: 🚨 session-state`: the timeout retry path must not expand a known transcript replay hazard where an aborted empty assistant leaf can remain before the trailing-user repair path.

This head includes the same transcript-safe repair from sibling PR #95766:

- drops an empty aborted assistant leaf before checking/repairing the trailing-user invariant;
- covers the helper behavior in `attempt.prompt-helpers.test.ts`;
- preserves the timeout retry behavior from this PR while avoiding an additional session-state replay risk.

## Real Behavior Proof

### Runtime proof: local OpenAI-compatible timeout service

I re-ran this PR through the actual embedded runtime, not only the helper. The proof uses:

- current PR head: `3414cee48409b1b4fe3b765e71b6ff493185f322`
- `openclaw agent --local` from this PR checkout
- a temporary isolated user home, OpenClaw config, state directory, and workspace
- a local OpenAI-compatible Responses service with its endpoint/port redacted
- synthetic model names: `timeout-primary` and `fallback-ok`
- no live gateway, no production state, no external provider call, and no real credentials

The local service intentionally holds the first two `timeout-primary` Responses requests past the configured 1 second provider timeout, then returns a valid streamed Responses success for `fallback-ok`.

Observed runtime request order:

```text
POST /v1/responses request #1 model=timeout-primary  -> provider timeout
POST /v1/responses request #2 model=timeout-primary  -> same model/profile retry before fallback
POST /v1/responses request #3 model=fallback-ok      -> streamed success
```

Observed final visible payload:

```text

```

Redacted runtime log excerpts:

```text

[agent/embedded] embedded run failover decision: stage=assistant decision=fallback_model reason=timeout from=openai/timeout-primary profile=- rawError=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_failed requested=openai/timeout-primary candidate=openai/timeout-primary reason=timeout next=openai/fallback-ok detail=LLM idle timeout (1s): no response from model
[model-fallback/decision] model fallback decision: decision=candidate_succeeded requested=openai/timeout-primary candidate=openai/fallback-ok reason=unknown next=none
```

Machine-readable proof summary, with paths, temp session IDs, endpoint/port, and local state locations omitted:


target.title: fix(discord): guard message-tool-only final delivery
target.body:
## Summary

Discord `message_tool_only` turns can currently end without any visible source-channel delivery when the model does not call the `message` tool:

- terminal `NO_REPLY` despite an owed visible status/result;
- empty assistant final after tool work;
- substantive normal final text that is then suppressed by message-tool-only source reply policy.

Prompt/tool-description guidance helps, but it is advisory. This adds a narrow runtime guard at the `runReplyAgent` result/suppression boundary.

## What changed

- Detect Discord `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` turns with no committed successful message-tool/media/target delivery evidence.
- For substantive final payloads, mark them with existing `deliverDespiteSourceReplySuppression` metadata so dispatch can surface them instead of silently suppressing them.
- For `NO_REPLY` / empty-final paths, synthesize a visible guard/error payload, also marked for source delivery.
- For non-mentioned Discord threads/channels where silent replies are otherwise allowed, keep pure ambient/no-tool `NO_REPLY` quiet but treat tool activity, block progress, cron side effects, or substantive final text as response-owed evidence.
- Also cover Discord tool/progress activity followed by empty/`NO_REPLY` finals when `sourceReplyDeliveryMode` is not `message_tool_only`; real thread traces showed that path can occur while visible progress/tool chatter is emitted but no final/status answer is delivered.
- Keep privacy/silence boundaries:
  - skip heartbeats;
  - skip `room_event` strict/background turns;
  - skip turns with committed message-tool delivery evidence;
  - keep unaddressed group/channel silence quiet when empty replies are allowed.

## Related context

This complements, rather than replaces, nearby work:

- #84022 — current Discord transcript-only/suppressed final class.
- #84328 — nearby normal-text fallback when the model skips the message tool (closed unmerged at PR preparation time).
- #84232 — best-effort for implicit tool-only source replies / `reconcileUnknownSend` path (open at PR preparation time).
- #82609 — merged strict `message_tool` policy baseline.
- #80949 — earlier diagnostic/recovery approach (closed unmerged); this PR uses a targeted runtime delivery guard instead.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: Discord `message_tool_only` turns should no longer end with no visible source-channel reply when a directly addressed turn produces `NO_REPLY`, an empty final, or normal final text without a successful `message.send`.
- **Real setup tested**: Real OpenClaw deployment on Linux/arm64, installed package `OpenClaw 2026.5.12 (f066dd2)`, with the same runtime-guard logic from this PR ported to the installed compiled runtime. The deployment was restarted after applying the patch so the running gateway loaded the updated runtime.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal group mention gating now has native mention metadata available, but the delivered-turn decision facts are only visible inside the Signal monitor. Downstream prompt/tool context cannot inspect whether the inbound group message had native mention metadata, whether `requireMention` was enforced for that delivered turn, or which mention path matched the bot. That makes native-only group behavior hard to debug and forces consumers to infer channel-specific facts from text.

## Summary

- Exposes Signal mention-gating facts on the generic inbound message context.
- Adds `CanDetectMention`, `HasAnyMention`, `EffectiveWasMentioned`, `MentionShouldSkip`, and `MentionSource` for delivered native/text mention decisions, while reusing the existing canonical `GroupRequireMention` field.
- Keeps the Signal mention source literal typed so SDK/context consumers can rely on `"native"` vs `"mention_pattern"`.

## Stack

This is stacked after #96738 (`fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating`). Until #96738 lands, this PR's diff will include that dependency.

## Production impact

No new outbound behavior. This only makes already-computed delivered-turn mention gating facts inspectable by prompts, tests, and plugin/channel contracts. Skipped Signal turns still return before prompt/tool context is built, so this PR intentionally does not expose a public skipped-turn context field.

target.title: fix(signal): detect native bot mentions in group gating
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal groups can be configured with `requireMention=true` so side chatter stays quiet until the bot is explicitly mentioned. Signal native mentions arrive as structured `dataMessage.mentions[]` metadata plus object-replacement characters in the message text. The current Signal handler renders those placeholders as `@<uuid>` or `@<phone>`, then relies on text mention regexes. Selecting the bot from Signal's native mention UI can therefore fail to wake the bot unless a matching text fallback happens to be configured.

This also leaves `canDetectMention` tied only to configured text regexes and passes `hasAnyMention=false` even when Signal supplied structured mention metadata.

## Why This Change Was Made

This patch keeps the fix inside the Signal plugin and adds a small native mention fact resolver. It compares structured Signal mention metadata against the current bot account identity:

- UUID via `channels.signal.accountUuid`
- phone number via the existing E.164 normalizer and `channels.signal.account`

The event handler now combines text fallback and native metadata:

- `wasMentioned` is true for text fallback or a native mention that targets the current bot account.
- `canDetectMention` reflects text regexes or available bot account identity.
- `hasAnyMention` reflects valid structured Signal mention metadata so the shared mention-decision contract can distinguish command bypass from messages mentioning someone else.

Mentions of other participants do not trigger the bot. Missing bot identity does not become a false mention. Existing text fallback, group access checks, pending history, attachment restraint, control-command handling, direct messages, and `requireMention=false` behavior stay unchanged.

This supersedes #69413, which was closed without merge, by adding the missing capability facts, event-handler coverage, and docs.

## User Impact

Before:

> A user could select the bot from Signal's native mention UI in a `requireMention` group and get no response because the rendered `@uuid`/`@phone` text did not match the configured agent-name regex.

After:

> Native Signal mentions targeting the current bot account pass mention gating. Mentions of other participants remain silent and are kept only as bounded pending context. A later bot mention can include recent skipped group context and reply in the same group.

Docs now describe Signal native mention behavior, `accountUuid`, text mention fallback, and a mention-gated group configuration with bounded history.

### Behavior Change

Signal groups with `requireMention=true` that have a configured bot identity (`accountUuid`/`account`) but no text mention regexes previously fell through to pass-through handling. After this change they enforce mention gating via native Signal mention metadata. Group chatter that did not mention the bot but previously reached it may now be gated. This is intended and makes native-only `requireMention` groups behave as documented. Maintainers with such groups should expect stricter, correct gating after upgrade.

### Trust Model

`dataMessage.mentions[]` is sender-supplied. A group member could craft metadata naming the bot; the only effect is waking the bot, which any member can already do via a normal Signal mention. Native facts are still validated against a real object-replacement placeholder span, so malformed metadata does not become a bot mention.

### Native Identity Note

For full native mention coverage, configure `channels.signal.accountUuid` alongside `channels.signal.account`. Phone-only identity can still match phone-backed mention metadata, but UUID-only Signal mention metadata requires `accountUuid`.

## Evidence

- Base: `4ecb45b chore: update default check gate expectations`
- Head: `83ac15c979a4`
- Static whitespace check: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD`
- Focused Signal mention-gating tests passed on this branch:
  `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/monitor/event-handler.mention-gating.test.ts`
- Production TypeScript check passed:
  `pnpm tsgo:prod`

The focused Signal suite covers:

- native bot UUID mention without text mention patterns;
- native bot phone mention with E.164 normalization;
- native mention of another participant stays silent and records pending context;
- malformed matching metadata does not become a bot mention;
- no-detector behavior remains explicit;
- helper facts for bot mention, unrelated mention, malformed span, and missing bot identity.

### Redacted Live Signal Proof

This is the sanitized inspectable artifact from a live 3-person private Signal smoke. IDs, UUIDs, phone numbers, group IDs, raw message bodies, and private participant context are intentionally omitted.

```text
environment: live private Signal group
runtime: OpenClaw gateway with this PR's Signal mention patch installed
config.runtime: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
config.template: { signalConfigured: true, groupPolicy: "allowlist", groupAllowFromCount: 1, groupsCount: 1, requireMentionGroups: 1, accountUuidSet: true, historyLimit: 3 }
signal.probe: { configured: true, running: true, probeOk: true, probeStatus: 200 }
session.markerScan: { proofMarker: "96738", markerFileCount: 11, rawContentPrinted: false }

case: native bot mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected the bot display name; no text mention regex fallback was used
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: true, shouldSkip: false }
observed: bot account replied in the same group with the controlled proof marker

case: native non-bot participant mention from Signal UI
input: Signal native mention picker selected another group participant, not the bot
delivery: Signal message info showed delivery to both the bot account and the mentioned participant
expected PR facts: { canDetectMention: true, hasAnyMention: true, wasMentioned: false, shouldSkip: true }
observed: no bot reply was produced after the quiet window
```

target.title: fix: clear session suspension timers on gateway shutdown
target.body:
Closes #101720

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where sessions suspended for quota or circuit reasons could leave lane auto-resume timers pending while the gateway was shutting down. Those timers could later call back into command lane concurrency after shutdown had already begun.

## Why This Change Was Made

The session-suspension module now owns a cleanup hook for pending lane auto-resume timers, and the gateway shutdown path invokes it after drain handling and before tearing down runtimes and background services. The change keeps normal TTL auto-resume behavior intact while preventing stale shutdown-time timer callbacks.

## User Impact

Gateway shutdown and restart are less likely to race with delayed session-suspension timers. Suspended lanes still auto-resume normally during regular runtime operation.

## Data Model / Upgrade Compatibility

No persisted schema or migration behavior changes. The production change only clears the in-memory `laneResumeTimers` map during gateway shutdown. Existing `quotaSuspension` entries remain schemaVersion 1 and are neither rewritten nor migrated by the new cleanup hook. The serialized-state surface ClawSweeper detected is test coverage around the existing session suspension shape, not a new stored field.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed, 2 Vitest shards.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed.
- `git diff --check` - passed.
- `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/session-suspension.ts src/gateway/server-close.ts src/agents/session-suspension.test.ts src/gateway/server-close.test.ts` - passed locally in child mode. Testbox delegation was blocked because the local Crabbox binary is 0.15.0 and the Testbox flow requires >=0.22.0; the local run also emitted Node 22.18.0 engine warnings.

## Real Behavior Proof

Ran a standalone Node/tsx proof that imports the real `suspendSession()`, real command queue state, real timers, and the real `createGatewayCloseHandler()` shutdown path. The control leg proves the pending auto-resume timer normally fires after TTL; the shutdown leg proves gateway close clears the pending timer so it cannot restore lane concurrency after teardown begins.

```text
$ node --import tsx --input-type=module <standalone #101720 shutdown proof>
OpenClaw #101720 runtime proof root: /var/folders/sx/2qmmyr8s7rz8m6d22p3htynw0000gn/T/openclaw-101720-proof-pZFur4
Using real suspendSession(), real timers, real command queue, and createGatewayCloseHandler().
control after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[session-suspension] auto-resumed lane after suspension TTL
control after ttl without shutdown: lane=main maxConcurrent=4 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after suspend: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
[shutdown] started: proof shutdown for #101720
shutdown drainActiveSessionsForShutdown reason=shutdown
[gmail-watcher] gmail watcher stopped
[shutdown] completed cleanly in 29ms
gateway close completed warnings=[] durationMs=29
shutdown case immediately after close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
shutdown case after ttl post-close: lane=main maxConcurrent=0 queued=0 active=0
```

The important behavior is the final line: after waiting longer than the suspension TTL after gateway close, the main lane remains suspended at `maxConcurrent=0`; in the control leg, the same TTL restores the lane to `maxConcurrent=4`.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`.
